---------------------------------------------- 287

1 
 
 
01. State of the Economy 
 
Uttar Pradesh, a symbol of India's cultural heritage and historical pride, is now advancing 
toward its goals with a renewed economic vision and energy. The state's economy reflects the 
aspirations of over 25 Crore citizens, positioning it as a major hub for agricultural production, 
industrial growth, and technological innovation. Spread across the fertile plains of the Ganga and 
Yamuna rivers, the state plays a leading role in the production of food grains, sugarcane, mangoes, 
milk, oilseeds, and potatoes-earning it the title of the nation's "food reservoir." Diligent farmers not 
only make the state self-reliant but also contribute significantly to ensuring national food security. 
The sugar industry, based on sugarcane, has established Uttar Pradesh as a prominent industrial 
centre on the global stage, ensuring balanced growth in both agriculture and industry. 
 
In recent years, Uttar Pradesh has made remarkable progress in the field of industrialization, 
emerging as a new destination of investment and development. The state has so far received 
investment proposals worth nearly Rs. 50 Lakh Crore, which reflects its economic strength and 
potential. As a result of the government’s farsighted vision, 34 effective policies have been 
implemented, providing industries with a favourable environment, better infrastructure, and a secure 
atmosphere for investors. This achievement is not only accelerating the state’s progress but also 
creating new employment opportunities, expanding modern technology, and strengthening Uttar 
Pradesh’s identity at the global level. Extensive development has taken place in sectors such as 
textiles, handicrafts, automobiles, and electronics. Kanpur, once called the “Manchester of the East,” 
still remains a major centre for leather and textile industries and is currently being developed as a 
Drone City, while Noida and Greater Noida have established themselves as important hubs for IT, 
manufacturing, and real estate. Similarly, Lucknow, enriched with policy reforms and infrastructural 
facilities, is being prepared to develop as an AI City. By evolving into an AI City, Lucknow will 
become a new centre of innovation and technological progress. Investments in digital infrastructure 
and the startup ecosystem have established the state as an emerging hub in the field of technology. 
 
Projects such as the Yamuna Expressway and the Industrial Development Authority have 
given rise to important infrastructure like the Jewar International Airport, which has strengthened 
the state’s connectivity and encouraged global investment. In addition, the Defence Industrial 
Corridor being developed in Uttar Pradesh is a significant initiative in the direction of promoting 
self-reliance and innovation. At the same time, the “One District One Product” (ODOP) scheme is 
empowering local industries by linking the unique potential of each district to the global supply chain.

2 
 
Uttar Pradesh is an invaluable repository of historical and spiritual heritage, where cities like 
Varanasi, Lucknow, and Agra present a unique confluence of traditional art, trade, and tourism, while 
Banarasi silk sarees, Lucknow’s Chikankari, and Moradabad’s brass industry stand as symbols of 
the state’s exquisite art and craftsmanship. These products not only strengthen local identity but also 
represent Indian culture and tradition at the global level. 
 
With the commitment of rapid development of the state, a target has been set to raise the 
economy to one trillion dollars. To achieve this objective, well-considered plans, development works, 
and new policies as required are being continuously implemented in all sectors of the economy. It is 
a reflection of meaningful developmental efforts that, according to quick estimates assessed at current 
prices, Uttar Pradesh’s Gross State Domestic Product, which was Rs. 13.30 Lakh Crore in 2016-17, 
steadily increased to Rs. 26.67 Lakh Crore in 2023-24. In the advance estimates for 2024-25, it was 
projected at Rs. 29.62 Lakh Crore, which in the revised advance estimates stood at Rs. 29.78 Lakh 
Crore. According to quick estimates prepared by incorporating comprehensive data, while 
maintaining the pace of development, the Gross State Domestic Product has been assessed at 
Rs.30.25 Lakh Crore with a growth of 13.4 percent compared to the previous year, exceeding both 
the earlier estimates. This increase in the economy has been possible due to performance surpassing 
expectations in manufacturing and financial services. 
 
According to the report of the State Bank of India’s research unit ‘Ecowrap’ India’s economy 
is moving towards becoming the world’s third-largest economy by the year 2027, surpassing Japan 
and Germany, and in this achievement, the role of Uttar Pradesh is considered decisive. 
 
 
 
In the year 2025-26, Uttar Pradesh’s economy is estimated to reach a level of about 
Rs 36 Lakh Crore. The basis of this projected achievement is the remarkable growth 
recorded in recent years across all major sectors such as agriculture, animal husbandry, 
fisheries, manufacturing, construction, tourism, financial services, trade, and real estate, 
which will provide the desired momentum in the coming year. At present, the pace of the 
economy is strong, supported by future-oriented plans, policy initiatives, and continuous 
investment inflows. The combined effect of all these efforts is providing greater stability 
to the state’s economic structure. Over the past eight years, the state has created a 
development-oriented environment, in which strong law and order, administrative reforms, 
and policy changes have been prominent. As a result of these reforms, the state has 
maintained continuity of high growth rates and has laid a solid foundation for relatively 
higher growth rates in the coming years.

Economic and Structural Profile 
Uttar Pradesh’s Gross State Domestic Product at current prices was Rs. 13.30 Lakh Crore in 
the financial year 
2016-17, 
which, 
growing 
at 
an 
annual compound 
rate of 10.8 percent 
over the past eight 
years, has increased 
to Rs. 30.25 Lakh 
Crore in the quick 
estimates for the 
financial year 202425 (Figure 1.1). 
According to the 
quick estimates for 
2024-25, the state’s economy is contributing 9.1 percent to the country’s total Gross Domestic 
Product. With the development-oriented approach adopted by the state government in recent years, 
it is fully anticipated that the regional economy will remain strong, and the state will successfully 
move towards the goal of O.T.D./Viksit Uttar Pradesh 2047. The state’s economy is estimated to 
reach Rs. 36 Lakh Crore in the financial year 2025-26. 
 
Structural changes in Uttar Pradesh’s economy are clearly visible from 2017-18 to 2024-25.

the primary sector

dependent on the service sector, Uttar Pradesh has adopted a path of balanced development by

 In the financial year 2024-25, the participation of various sub-sectors in the state’s economy 
shows that agriculture, forestry, and fisheries contribute 24.9%, reflecting the rural strength and food 
security of the state. At the same time, construction (12.9%) and real estate & professional services 
(13.9%) highlight the direction of rapid urbanization and development. Manufacturing (11.7%), trade 
& hotels (8.3%), and transport & communication (7.4%) underscore industrial progress and the 
robustness of the service sector. Meanwhile, financial services (3.7%) and public administration 
(5.8%) strengthen the foundations of economic stability and good governance (Figure 1.3). Although 
the state’s economy is based on agriculture, it is achieving balanced growth in industry, construction, 
and service sectors, which signals sustainable and inclusive progress in the future. 
 
Sector-wise Comparative Scenario of the Economy 
The sector-wise comparative scenario of the state’s economy highlights its progress and 
balanced development. The agriculture sector, with its strong productive capacity, is strengthening 
food security and rural livelihoods. The industrial sector is gaining new momentum through 
investment, manufacturing, and expansion of infrastructure. Meanwhile, the service sector 
comprising the growing contributions of trade, transport, financial services, and real estate is 
providing the economy with a modern, diversified, and employment-generating direction.

The slight decline in the quick estimates was due to the sub-sectors of animal husbandry and forestry,

and revised advance estimates. 
The progressive growth of agriculture and allied sectors not only reflects continuous 
improvement in agricultural production capacity, but also highlights the active contribution of allied 
areas such as livestock, forestry, and fisheries. This steadily rising growth is evidence of lasting 
improvements in the state’s food security, employment generation, and rural income, which further 
strengthens the path toward sustainable and inclusive development in the future.

In the financial year 2024-25, Uttar Pradesh’s total foodgrain production increased by 9.9% 
compared to the previous year, reaching 737.4 Lakh metric tons, thereby securing a leading position 
in the country. Among the crops, the highest growth rate was recorded in oilseeds at 57.9%, followed 
by total cereals at 11%, within which rice production rose by 23.6% and wheat production by 6.3%. 
Maize, pulses, and sugarcane also registered notable increases. Improvements were also recorded in 
irrigated area, crop intensity, and Gross Value Added per hectare. Over the past eight years, fisheries 
and aquaculture have grown by 115.5%, milk production has risen by 33.6% placing the state first in 
the country and egg production has increased by 167%. In 2025-26, fish production is expected to 
grow by an additional 15.7%, reflecting the state’s efforts toward sustainable agricultural 
development and diversification. 
Under the Uttar Pradesh Food Processing Industry Policy-2023 and the Pradhan Mantri 
Micro Food Industry Upgradation Scheme, the food processing industry is being promoted through 
financial concessions of 35-50% on agricultural produce processing, export capacity enhancement, 
establishment/modernization of units, value addition, and cold chain infrastructure, along with a 35% 
grant for small enterprises. The Government of Uttar Pradesh is establishing advanced seed parks in 
five agro-climatic zones, equipped with facilities for seed processing, speed breeding, and hybrid 
seed development. This will reduce dependence on seed imports, increase productivity, raise farmers’ 
incomes, and move the state towards becoming India’s leading seed production hub. For the 
upgradation of the agricultural sector, a Seed Policy has been proposed for Uttar Pradesh. Its 
objectives are to provide farmers with timely access to high-quality seeds, increase the seed 
replacement rate, encourage crop diversification, promote hybrid seed production and research, and 
empower Farmer Producer Organizations (FPOs) and small entrepreneurs to build an effective seed 
ecosystem.

To establish integrated industrial areas across all districts, the Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel 
Employment and Industrial Area Scheme was launched. Under this scheme, the Department of 
Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSME) will develop industrial and employment zones in 
each district. All assistance and facilities for entrepreneurs will be provided under one roof, including 
common facility Centres, testing facilities, product display and design Centres, training Centres, 
financing, and offices of all relevant government departments and financial institutions. Additionally, 
plug-and-play industrial plots will be set up within these zones, enabling entrepreneurs to access all 
technical and financial support in one place and establish their projects directly at the site. This 
scheme is a major initiative aimed at making Uttar Pradesh industrially strong and self-reliant, with 
the objectives of promoting industrial development, generating employment at the local level, and 
integrating training with entrepreneurship. 
Integrated Manufacturing and Logistics Clusters (IMLCs) are being developed along 
the IMLC Expressway in the state as major industrial hubs. Their primary objective is to bring 
industries, manufacturing units, and logistics services together at one location, making production 
and supply chains more efficient, faster, and cost-effective. Under the IMLC initiative, across 26 
districts, 29 IMLC complexes are planned, of which land acquisition has already been completed for 
27 complexes, covering 84 percent of the required area. The development of IMLCs will transform 
industrial clusters into modern, multimodal, and technology-driven logistics ecosystems. This will 
accelerate the state’s industrial and export sectors while also promoting local-level employment 
generation

benefiting beneficiaries and youth from the divisions of Meerut, Saharanpur, Aligarh, and Agra. 
Capital expenditure in Uttar Pradesh has been consistently increasing to accelerate 
infrastructure development. In Varanasi, the country’s first urban ropeway project is under 
construction, considered a historic step in urban transport. The state is emerging as the capital of 
expressways, with 7 expressways operational, 3 under construction, and 12 proposed. Aviation 
infrastructure is expanding rapidly. At present, the state has 12 domestic and 4 international 
airports (Lucknow, Varanasi, Kushinagar, and Ayodhya). The construction of the Noida 
International Greenfield Airport at Jewar, Gautam Buddha Nagar, is nearing completion. Once 
operational, Uttar Pradesh will become the first state in the country to have 5 international airports.

Promoting a Development- Conducive Environment with Robust 
Law and Order 
On one hand, Uttar Pradesh has created a development-oriented environment through rapid 
economic growth and investment attraction, while on the other hand, it has established a regime of 
strong law and order to ensure crime control and public safety. This balanced approach is 
continuously propelling the state towards the goal of ‘Developed India, Developed Uttar Pradesh @ 
2047.’ 
The state government has accorded top priority to strengthening law and order. Strict action 
against organized crime and mafia networks has led to a significant decline in crime rates, thereby 
increasing investor confidence. Modern technology-based policing, CCTV surveillance, and digital 
case management systems have given new direction to police reforms. Emphasis on the registration 
of offenders has fostered an environment where citizens feel confident to lodge complaints without 
fear. 
Uttar Pradesh at the Forefront of Compliance Reduction 
 Securing first place at the national level in January 2026 under Deregulation Phase-I, conducted 
under the leadership of the Cabinet Secretariat of the Government of India, is a major 
achievement of Uttar Pradesh’s administrative reforms and investment-friendly policy 
framework. This success propels Uttar Pradesh beyond Ease of Doing Business towards TrustBased Governance. 
 The Government of Uttar Pradesh identified and rationalized existing regulatory complexities at 
every stage of the investment lifecycle land allocation, construction, operation, and expansion. 
Reforms related to land, construction, labour, environment, fire safety, utilities, and governance 
systems resulted in reduced approval timelines, lower transaction costs, and increased 
regulatory predictability. Consequently, projects are being expedited from conception to 
operation. 
 Through legislative amendments, including the Uttar Pradesh Facilitation of Business 
(Amendment of Provisions) Act, 2025, the state institutionalized decriminalization and 
deregulation. Under this, more than 40 provisions across 10 state Acts were amended, 200 
compliances were removed from the scope of criminal liability, and nearly 90% of minor 
offenses now carry only monetary penalties instead of imprisonment. 
 Under Single-Window and Digital Governance, all major departmental services of the state 
have been integrated into the single-window system, which is being upgraded as Investor Mitra 
3.0. This portal will provide investors with end-to-end online tracking, defined service timelines, 
and seamless integration with the National Single Window System. By reducing unnecessary 
procedures, the number of services across more than 40 departments has been cut from 530 to 
fewer than 200. This process has led to significant reductions in form fields, document checklists, 
and procedural steps. 
 To remove traditional barriers related to land use and zoning, Uttar Pradesh has implemented the 
Model Building Construction and Development Byelaws-2025.

24 
 The process of land use conversion has been simplified and fully digitized. Under this, the 
GIS-based Industrial Land Bank has been linked with the India Industrial Land Bank (IILB), 
providing investors with advance information on land availability and infrastructure readiness 
across more than 300 industrial areas, including UPSIDA, NOIDA, GNIDA, YEIDA, and 
UPEIDA.

 By adopting a risk-based approach in environmental, fire, and safety approvals, unnecessary

To strengthen women’s safety, a zero-tolerance policy against crime has been implemented. 
Under the Safe City Project, the deployment of women police beats, an extensive CCTV network,

For judicial support, the establishment of fast-track courts and e-courts has accelerated the

and industry. As a result of these efforts, the state has emerged as a centre of record investment and

Uttar Pradesh has now become a state with a modern, digital, and trust-based regulatory

Next Gen GST Reform 2.0: The Dawn of a New Economic Era 
GST Reform 2.0, implemented nationwide from 22 September 2025, ushered the 
tax system into a new economic era. The 12% and 28% rates were abolished, 
leaving only 5% and 18%. As a result, essential goods are taxed at 0-5%, common 
goods at 5%, and luxury and sin goods at higher rates. This has enhanced the 
purchasing power of the common man, farmers, small entrepreneurs, and the 
middle class. Taxes on health insurance, medicines, and cancer treatment have 
been eliminated, while taxes on medical oxygen and spectacles have been 
reduced to 5%. Automobiles, refrigerators, and air conditioners are capped at 
18%, providing relief to the middle class. For farmers, GST on tractors, drip 
irrigation, and sprinkler equipment has been reduced to 5%, strengthening their 
income and the agricultural economy. For trade and MSMEs, return filing and 
registration have been simplified, input tax issues resolved, and exporters are now 
entitled to 90% tax refunds within seven days. Thus, GST Reform 2.0 has 
provided relief to the public, support to farmers, convenience to the middle class, 
and new energy to small businesses, giving India’s economy a progressive 
direction.

The most important indicator for assessing the financial position of any State is the 
percentage of fiscal deficit to GSDP. It reflects the excess of total expenditure over total receipts, 
which is met by borrowings. This leads to an increase in the Government’s overall liabilities. In the 
first year of the 15th Finance Commission, i.e., 2020-21, it was kept within 3 percent of GSDP. Due 
to the adverse impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on the resources of both the State and the Centre, 
the Central Government permitted the State Governments an additional borrowing limit of 2 percent 
of GSDP, i.e., a total limit of 5 percent for the year 2020-21. Accordingly, the FRBM Act, 2004 of 
Uttar Pradesh was amended for the year 2020-21 to raise the fiscal deficit limit from 3 percent to 5 
percent of GSDP. Based on the actual estimates of the financial year 2023-24 and the provisional 
estimates of GSDP, the State’s fiscal deficit remained within the prescribed limit, at 3.0 percent of 
GSDP. On the basis of the revised estimates for the financial year 2024-25 and the quick estimates 
of GSDP, the State’s fiscal deficit was 3.1 percent of GSDP. For the year 2025-26, the fiscal deficit 
is estimated to remain within the prescribed limit. 
 
According to the NITI Aayog report (2014-15 to 2022-23), Uttar Pradesh has been placed in 
the leading category among States in terms of fiscal position. During this period, the composite Fiscal 
Health Index increased from 37.0 to 45.9, indicating a remarkable improvement in the quality of 
expenditure. The State’s fiscal deficit remained within the prescribed limit, while revenue surplus 
and primary savings resulted in a reduction in public debt as a proportion of Gross State Domestic 
Product. The augmentation of internal resources, rising expenditure on development and health 
services, and the decline in debt burden present clear evidence of the strong, responsible, and 
balanced financial management of the State Government.

03. Land and Forest Resources 
Uttar Pradesh, being the most populous and agriculturally significant State in the country, 
holds a special position with respect to its land and forest resources. Land and forest resources, while 
serving as the main foundation of agriculture, also play a central role in the State’s economic 
development, rural livelihoods, and social structure. According to the quick estimates for 2024-25, 
the forestry and logging sub-sector contributed 1.1 percent to the State’s Gross Value Added. In 
recent years, the Government has been implementing various programmes for the development of 
land and forest resources in the State, with the objective of conserving and enhancing the State’s 
geographical, natural, and biodiversity wealth, as well as promoting tourism. These efforts aim to 
ensure inclusive development of land, forest, and environment while safeguarding them. This chapter 
presents an economic review and analytical assessment of the underlying elements of the State’s land 
and forest resources, providing comprehensive insights in this context. 
3.1 Land Resources in the State 
Land resources are the main foundation of agriculture, animal husbandry, forest-based 
industrial products, water resources, tourism, environmental services, and rural livelihoods. Amid 
the rapidly changing economic landscape of the State and the vision of a developed Uttar Pradesh,

recognition of the doubling of tiger numbers, the Pilibhit Tiger Reserve was conferred the

3.1.1 Geographical Structure 
Geographically, Uttar Pradesh is the fourth largest State in the country, with a total 
geographical area of about 240,928 sq. km, and it is also the most populous State. The State extends 
from the foothills of the Himalayas in the north to the Vindhya mountain range in the south, which 
is highly fertile, water-rich, and suitable for agriculture. The central Ganga plain region, formed by 
the fertile soil brought by rivers, is the hub of foodgrain production. Bundelkhand is a dry region 
where land erosion and water scarcity are challenging problems; in view of this, the Government has 
been implementing schemes such as Amrit Sarovar to restore new and old ponds. The Vindhya 
region, on the other hand, is important for mixed farming and forests. Due to the diverse geographical 
features, the nature and utilization of land resources also vary. On the basis of climate and ecology, 
the State can be divided into nine categories for geographical economic analysis.

3.1.3 Land Reforms 
Different types of land are found in various regions of Uttar Pradesh, which also influence crop 
productivity. Subsidized programs are being implemented to improve soil health, including soil 
testing, integration of modern agricultural techniques, nutrient management, and the use of biofertilizers, all of which are contributing to enhanced land productivity. In addition, for land reforms, 
the schemes operated by the Department of Land Resources at the national level have been effectively 
implemented by the state government. 
 In accordance with the directives of the Government of India, from December 2023 the Unique 
Land Parcel Identification Number (ULPIN) system has been implemented in the state, under 
which a 14-digit alphanumeric unique ID is generated for each parcel of land. This complies with 
the international standards of the Electronic Commerce Code Management Association. Through 
this, efforts are being made to enable quick identification of land resources for disaster 
management, purchase and sale of land properties, and property taxation, as well as to bring 
transparency in real estate transactions and curb land mafias.

Finance Scheme aimed at increasing farmers’ income. Through this scheme, in addition to

Advisory. Farmers are proposed to be paid USD 6 per carbon credit every five years. As

49.05 Lakh have already been distributed to 239 farmers, and an additional Rs. 25.00 Lakh 
has been transferred to the Dudhwa Tiger Conservation Foundation.

3.2.4 Agro Forestry 
Under agro-forestry, the State Government is encouraging farmers to grow trees along with 
agricultural crops on the same land. This practice not only provides economic benefits to farmers but 
also strengthens them socially. To provide relief from the economic losses caused by natural disasters 
such as floods and droughts, emphasis is being laid on adopting this method in a practical manner. 
By adopting agro-forestry, farmers in the State are diversifying their cultivation. Alongside food 
grains, they are meeting their household needs by obtaining fuelwood, timber for agricultural tools, 
fodder for livestock, and other essentials from fields near their residences. In doing so, they are also 
strengthening their economic condition. 
 
3.2.5 Efforts for Biodiversity in the State 
 The State, with its diverse geographical structure and climate, is rich in biodiversity and 
wildlife. To conserve and enhance various species of animals, birds, and wildlife, establishments 
such as Dudhwa National Park, Tiger Reserves, Bird Sanctuaries, Wildlife Sanctuaries, and 
Zoological Parks have been set up. 
 
 The Pilibhit Tiger Reserve was honoured with the TX-2 Award for its remarkable 
achievement in doubling the tiger population. 
 According to the first nationwide dolphin census (2024) conducted by the Wildlife Institute 
of India, out of the country’s total 6,327 dolphins, the highest number, 2,397 dolphins, were 
found in Uttar Pradesh, reflecting the State’s commitment to river ecosystem conservation. 
 As another significant step in wildlife conservation, on 19 October 2022, an area of about 
53,000 hectares in the Vindhya mountain range of Chitrakoot district was notified as the 
Ranipur Tiger Reserve, making it the fourth tiger reserve of Uttar Pradesh. 
 In 2024, the State established the Jatayu Conservation and Breeding Centre in the 
Campierganj Range of Gorakhpur district. This is the country’s first dedicated breeding 
centre for the Red-headed Vulture.

The tiger is an integral part of wildlife heritage and culture, and the State Government is making 
remarkable efforts for its conservation and development through the use of modern technologies.

 For effective control of industrial pollution, air pollution control systems are being installed in 
identified polluting industrial units, with regular inspection of pollution control plants and 
monitoring of gaseous emissions. 
 In building construction projects, to control dust emissions generated during construction, 
conditions have been imposed in the No Objection Certificate requiring construction areas to be 
kept covered, water sprinkling, and installation of PTZ cameras and anti-smog guns at major 
sites. 
 In Uttar Pradesh, for prevention and control of air pollution, the country’s first air-shed based 
“Uttar Pradesh Clean Air Management Project” is being implemented with the support of the 
World Bank. Under this project, a loan of Rs. 2,658.09 Crore will be taken from the World Bank, 
along with a grant of Rs. 83.44 Crore. 
 Under the National Clean Air Programme (NCAP), action plans are being implemented in 17 
identified cities of the State. Responsibilities of 20 departments have been defined under this 
plan. The Uttar Pradesh Pollution Control Board is monitoring ambient air quality at 128 
locations across the State. 
 According to the Central Pollution Control Board, New Delhi, on the ‘PRANA’ portal, air quality 
in the 17 cities of the State has shown improvement in particulate matter ranging from 9 percent 
to 73 percent between 2019-20 and 2024-25. 
 For improvement of water quality in 17 identified polluted river stretches, action plans are being 
implemented. Under the National Water Quality Monitoring Programme, the Uttar Pradesh 
Pollution Control Board is monitoring rivers, ponds, and groundwater at 160 points. As a result 
of these action plans, Biological Oxygen Demand (BOD) in these river stretches has reduced by 
0.26 percent to 78 percent between 2019-20 and 2024-25. 
 The Uttar Pradesh Pollution Control Board is registering plastic manufacturing units and 
recyclers on the nationwide integrated EPR portal. 
 For effective disposal of domestic solid waste, the capacity of solid waste management facilities 
has been enhanced. From 5,395 tons per day in 2020, the capacity has increased to 19,130 tons 
per day in 2025. Similarly, sewage treatment capacities have been expanded, with 105 STPs 
(2,876.33 MLD) in 2020 increased to 155 STPs (4,705 MLD) in 2025. 
 In the National Capital Region (NCR) of Uttar Pradesh, to address air pollution, a Revised 
Graded Response Action Plan (GRAP) has been prepared. At present, 44 hot-mix plants are 
operating in NCR-UP, regulated as per the Air Quality Index under GRAP. For quick resolution 
of air pollution-related complaints in NCR, the ‘Self Declaration: Dust Control Audit App’ and 
the ‘Swachh Vayu App’ (Clean Air App) have been developed. Currently, 17 manual and 18 
real-time air quality monitoring stations are operational in the NCR region.

14,000 MW from utility-scale/solar parks, and 2,000 MW from the PM-KUSUM scheme.

04. Banking and Institutional Finance 
 
In the diverse and fast-evolving economy of Uttar Pradesh, the banking system and 
institutional financial architecture have emerged as a critical pillar of structural strength and stability. 
By deepening financial inclusion across rural and urban regions alike, the sector is enabling millions 
of citizens to access savings, credit, insurance, and investment services thereby fostering broad-based 
economic empowerment. In line with the State’s commitment to expanding and simplifying banking 
services and extending their reach from major urban centres to the most remote rural areas, banks 
and institutional financial institutions assume an increasingly strategic role. Through efficient 
allocation of resources, prudent risk management, and orderly cash flows, they reinforce 
macroeconomic stability and support sustained growth. The State continues to actively promote 
investment, facilitate the establishment of new industries, and revive existing enterprises. These 
efforts have accelerated economic activity, strengthened sectoral linkages, and contributed to more 
balanced and comprehensive development. Simultaneously, rising investments in education, 
healthcare, and other social sectors are ensuring that economic advancement is complemented by 
social progress. As a result, Uttar Pradesh is not only advancing toward higher growth trajectories 
but is also laying a robust, inclusive, and sustainable foundation for long-term prosperity. 
Under the Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana, Uttar Pradesh has secured the first position 
in the country by opening 10.22 Crore accounts by December 2025. Alongside this, the state also 
holds the top position nationwide under the Stand-Up India Scheme. Thus, as a result of financial 
inclusion, Uttar Pradesh is making a meaningful contribution to the nation’s progress while 
advancing towards comprehensive development. 
The State has significantly strengthened its banking infrastructure by establishing 4.50 Lakh
banking centres up to December 2025, ensuring service availability on average within every 
0.55 sq. km. This expansion has improved financial access, with the population served per 
branch declining to 11,565. 
Under the Annual Credit Plan for FY 2025-26, a credit disbursement target of Rs. 6.45 Lakh
Crore has been set, which is 24.52% higher than the previous year. Against this target, Rs.4.25
Lakh Crore has already been disbursed up to December 2025. 
Under the Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana, Uttar Pradesh has opened 10.22 Crore Jan Dhan
accounts as of December 2025, securing the first position in the country with a 17.76% share
out of the total 57.49 Crore accounts nationwide. 
The State’s overall Credit-Deposit (CD) ratio has increased from 59.04 in March 2025 to
60.39 in December 2025, reflecting stability and gradual improvement in credit expansion 
within the banking system. 
Under the “Your Capital, Your Rights” campaign, through camps organized across the
State, an unclaimed amount of Rs. 52.48 Crore in 6,525 accounts has been successfully settled
so far, marking a significant achievement in returning rightful funds to citizens.

Financial Inclusion 
The essence of financial inclusion is to ensure access to financial services for all sections of 
society, including savings and transaction accounts, low-cost loans for various purposes, financial 
counselling, and facilities such as life and non-life insurance. It fosters a culture of savings among 
rural and low-income groups, thereby strengthening the resource base of the financial system and 
accelerating economic growth. Moreover, by connecting people with formal banking, it safeguards 
their assets and resources. Thus, financial inclusion provides financial self-reliance, serving as the 
foundation for individual empowerment and holistic development.

3. Expansion of the Digital Payment Ecosystem 
 
This is a technological system that facilitates financial transactions through internet or mobilebased services. It includes digital wallets, bank transfers, payments via email or mobile applications, 
online shopping, e-banking, and digital currency. It helps in financial transactions in a secure, fast, 
and convenient manner, thereby improving financial inclusion. To expand and strengthen the digital 
payment ecosystem in the state, in the first phase two districts-Firozabad and Siddharth Nagar were 
identified on a pilot basis and fully digitized. In the second phase, two districts Sitapur and 
Moradabad were identified through their lead banks and digitized. As per the directives of the 
Reserve Bank of India, each lead bank was tasked with digitizing one district. Accordingly, eight 
districts-Fatehpur, Kannauj, Amroha, Deoria, Bahraich, Shamli, Maharajganj, and Varanasi were 
identified to expand and strengthen the digital payment ecosystem. Extending the above program, all 
districts of the state were earmarked for digitization. In October 2024, with the active contribution 
and support of all stakeholders, every district of the state was fully digitized. 
 
4. Financial Literacy 
Financial literacy means making society aware of financial subjects such as budgeting, 
investment, and banking-related issues, so that common people can easily make suitable financial 
decisions. To enhance financial literacy in the state, at present 281 Financial Literacy Centres are 
being operated. Through these Centres, during the financial year 2024-25 up to March 2025, a total 
of 30,022 camps were organized, providing financial literacy to 9.66 Lakh participants across 825 
identified blocks.

3. Atal Pension Yojana (APY) 
 
The Atal Pension Yojana (APY) is one of the flagship schemes of the Government of India. 
Its objective is to provide pension benefits to individuals in the unorganized sector, specifically those 
aged between 18 and 40 years. The scheme has significantly promoted personal financial security in 
Indian society. Through this scheme, even those working in the unorganized sector can receive a 
regular pension in old age by making consistent contributions during their working years. It serves 
as an important support system in making people self-reliant during their later years. For the financial 
year 2025-26, against the target of 16.48 Lakhs enrolments, a total of 14.77 Lakhs enrolments had 
been achieved by December 2025, thereby accomplishing 89.65% of the target.

has rationalized the pre-determined 75 indicators and implemented ABP+ with a total of 50 
indicators, based on 40 national and 10 state priority indicators. Among these, for 108 aspirational 
development blocks across 42 districts, a financial inclusion-related indicator, “Number of Banking 
Touch Points (Bank branches, BCs, IPPB Centres) located in the block”, has been included to ensure 
that every citizen has access to banking facilities. The baseline for this indicator is based on data as 
of 31.03.2023, and monthly progress reports are being uploaded on the Planning Department’s portal

Compared to 2016-17, in 2024-25 the contribution of agriculture and allied sectors to the state
economy rose from 23.9% to 24.9%. During this period, fisheries and aquaculture recorded 
the highest CAGR of 22.4%, followed by crops (11.8%), forestry (8.4%), and livestock 
(9.4%), reflecting farmer-friendly policies, irrigation expansion, MSP assurance, and 
promotion of fisheries. 
The Gross State Value Added (GSVA) from agriculture and allied sectors grew at 11.2% 
CAGR between 2016-17 and 2024-25, exceeding the national CAGR of 9.96%. 
In 2024-25, with foodgrain output of 737.4 Lakh MT, the state emerged as a leading producer.
Between 2016-17 and 2024-25, foodgrain production rose 32% and productivity 18.2%, 
raising the state’s share in national output from 20.3% to 20.6%. 
Between 2016-17 and 2024-25, Oilseed and maize production grew at CAGRs of 14.4% and 
9.1% respectively, showing diversification from wheat and rice toward oilseeds and coarse 
grains (millets). 
Irrigated area expanded about 12% from 2023-24, reaching 2.76 Crore ha in 2024-25. For
irrigation and water management, 150 projects were operational in 2017-18; under the One
Trillion Dollar Mission, 233 of 864 targeted projects were completed by 2025-26. 
Crop intensity rose 6.4% from 2023-24, reaching 193.66% in 2024-25, due to irrigation 
expansion, crop insurance, DigiCrop surveys, and reform policies. 
GVA per hectare of crops increased from Rs. 0.98 Lakh (2017-18) to Rs. 1.73 Lakh (202425). 
Efforts toward diversification are evident in 2025-26 estimates: oilseed and pulse areas 
expanded 17.2% and 13.6%, with production gains of 31.2% and 21.2%. 
Sugarcane output rose 56.3% from 2016-17, reaching 2453.46 Lakh MT in 2024-25,
contributing nearly 54% of national production. 
In 2024-25, horticultural output stood at 603.04 Lakh MT, giving the state a 16.3% share of 
national production. 
Livestock GVA rose from Rs. 0.84 Lakh Crore (2016-17) to Rs. 1.72 Lakh Crore (2024-25).
Uttar Pradesh contributes 15.66% to national milk output, ranking first in production. 
Fish production rose from 6.2 Lakh MT in 2016-17 to 13.31 Lakh MT in 2024-25, an increase
of 115.5%. 
GVA from fisheries and aquaculture rose from Rs. 4.78 thousand Crore (2016-17) to Rs.
24.09 thousand Crore (2024-25). 
In 2025-26, fish production grew another 15.7%, continuing the upward trend.

Uttar Pradesh is a state with an agriculture-based economy, where nearly 68 percent of the 
population is engaged in agricultural activities. In recent years, the remarkable progress achieved 
through continuous growth in agriculture and allied sectors can largely be attributed to productivity 
enhancement, crop diversification, and government policies that encourage the application of modern 
technologies. As a result of the sustained positive efforts of farmers and the government, the 
agricultural sector has made the state self-reliant in food security, moving towards a position of 
‘surplus beyond necessity.’ With a contribution of about 20 percent to the country’s total foodgrain 
production, Uttar Pradesh ranks first. Similarly, the state also holds the top position in the production 
of sugarcane, milk, potato, and mentha. Through farsighted and integrated strategic efforts by both 
the central and state governments, focusing on farmers, livestock rearers, and fishers, the state is 
advancing rapidly on the path of progress with the long-term vision of ‘Viksit Uttar Pradesh- Samarth 
Uttar Pradesh 2047’. 
5.1 Agriculture and Allied Sectors 
Agriculture, horticulture, animal husbandry, and fisheries serve as the lifeline of the state’s 
economic development. Along with providing raw materials for industrial sectors, agriculture and 
allied activities also ensure foodgrain production, thereby meeting the food security needs of the 
state’s growing population and serving as a vital source of livelihood.

of 25.6 percent, while the crop segment recorded 12.5 percent, forestry 9.1 percent, and livestock 8.2 
percent. This trend indicates that, alongside traditional crops, the contribution of allied sectors such

5.1.4 Land Reforms 
To enhance soil fertility, along with promoting organic farming in the state, cow-based natural 
farming was initiated in 2022-23 across 2,3,500 hectares in seven districts of Bundelkhand. This 
initiative has since been expanded to 26 districts located within a 5-kilometre stretch on both sides 
of the Ganga River, as well as to another 23 districts of the state. 
With the help of the Government of India, the state has introduced the ‘Bhu-Aadhaar or 
Unique Land Parcel Identification Number (ULPIN) system’ for proper land management. This 
system has not only facilitated convenient real estate transactions but has also demonstrated 
constructive improvements in property taxation, disaster planning, and response efforts. 
Through the Agriculture Department, a gypsum distribution scheme is being implemented in 
the state to address the deficiency of micronutrients in the soil and to promote land improvement. 
Under the Soil Health Card distribution scheme, 225.44 Lakh soil health cards were distributed 
between year 2017-18 and 2024-25 for regular testing of soil fertility. In year 2024-25, 9,862.34 
metric tons of agriculture-grade gypsum were supplied across 31 districts of the state. In addition, 
under the “Pt. Deen Dayal Kisan Samriddhi Yojana”, the state government made significant efforts, 
and during the period from year 2017-18 to year 2024-25, 2.78 Lakh hectares of land were improved 
and made cultivable. By December 2025, in the year 2025-26, land improvement was carried out 
over 34,345 hectares.

Uttar Pradesh Seed Policy 
With the objective of ensuring the availability of quality seeds to farmers, and to make the state 
self-reliant in seed production while promoting seed research, the Government of Uttar Pradesh has 
proposed the Uttar Pradesh Seed Policy. 
The goal of this policy is to ensure that every farmer has timely access to sufficient quantities of 
high-quality seeds and planting material of improved varieties at fair prices. This will help increase 
the seed replacement rate and bring about a revolutionary transformation in the agricultural 
production landscape of the state. 
Targets: 
 To make Uttar Pradesh self-reliant in the production of high-quality and high-yielding seed 
varieties for agriculture and allied sectors, while also creating an effective seed ecosystem in the 
state. 
 Taking into account the crop diversification strategy, to promote the production of seeds and 
planting material for oilseeds, pulses, coarse cereals, maize, horticultural crops, and fodder, 
thereby increasing farmers’ incomes, improving the overall economy, and achieving the targets 
of Gross State Value Added in the agricultural sector. 
 To promote the production of hybrid seeds and planting material, with enhanced efforts in 
training and capacity building of seed producers. 
 To strengthen community-managed seed production systems for empowering Farmer Producer 
Organizations and small entrepreneurs. 
 To encourage research for the development of high-yielding seed varieties specific to agroclimatic zones of the state, ensuring increased productivity.

5.5 Livestock 
Uttar Pradesh is the state with the largest livestock population in the country. Animal 
husbandry acts as an important catalyst for the economic and social development of the agriculturerelated sector. Nearly 70 percent of the state’s population still resides in villages, and agriculturebased activities remain their primary source of livelihood. Since more than 70 percent of farmers 
have small landholdings, animal husbandry is the best option for the majority of farmers alongside 
agriculture, as it provides them with a regular and assured income even on small plots of land. In 
view of this, the allocation for animal husbandry-related schemes has been significantly increased 
from Rs. 1,37,423.53 Lakh approved in year 2017-18 to Rs. 4,11,530.86 Lakh approved in year 202425. 
Food Processing: An Emerging Industry 
Uttar Pradesh Food Processing Industry Policy - 2023 
To promote the processing of agricultural produce and enhance export potential, this policy was 
implemented in February 2023. To attract investors and producers, the following incentives have been 
provided: 
For the establishment of food processing units, a rebate of 35 percent of the cost of plant, 
machinery, and technical civil works, up to a maximum of Rs. 5 Crore, will be granted. For 
expansion, modernization, or upgradation of food processing units, a rebate of 35 percent of the 
cost of plant, machinery, and technical civil works, up to a maximum of Rs. 1 Crore, will be 
provided. 
For value addition and cold chain infrastructure (storage, pack houses, pre-cooling units, ripening 
chambers, transport infrastructure), 35 percent support is admissible. For frozen storage/deep 
freezers, value addition and processing infrastructure, and irradiation facilities, 50 percent of the 
project cost up to a maximum of Rs. 10 Crore is permissible.

6.3 Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana: Smokeless Fuel in Every 
Kitchen- Illuminating Happiness Among Women 
The government has fulfilled its commitment to provide clean fuel to poor families by 
implementing this welfare scheme. Under the Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana, free gas connections 
are being provided in the name of the woman of the household. Each beneficiary of the scheme 
receives LPG cylinders at Rs. 840 per cylinder, against which a subsidy of Rs. 335.19 is directly 
credited to their bank account. 
In addition, two free cylinder refills are provided every year with the objective of promoting 
the use of LPG and fostering the habit of adopting clean fuel. Under the scheme, in the first phase of 
2024-25 (from October 1, 2024 to December 31, 2024), 88.60 Lakh beneficiaries received free refill 
cylinders, while in the second phase (from January 1, 2025 to March 31, 2025), 90.36 Lakh 
beneficiaries were covered. In the first phase of 2025-26 (from October 1, 2025 to December 31, 
2025), 89.44 Lakh beneficiaries received free refill cylinders. 
Since the commencement of the scheme in the year 2018-19, 185 Lakh Ujjwala gas 
connections have been provided so far. This scheme has proved to be a milestone from the point of 
view of the health and convenience of targeted eligible families, especially rural women. Through 
this scheme, while the social dignity of women has increased, there has also been a rise in the use of 
clean fuel among women, and the availability of smoke-free kitchens has relieved them from the 
harmful effects on their health.

System

a system whereby the woman of the household is considered the head of the family, and ration cards 
are issued in her name. In addition, priority is given to women’s self-help groups in the allocation of 
Public Distribution System (PDS) shops. This decision marks a significant step toward women’s 
empowerment, enabling them to become self-reliant and fostering entrepreneurship. As of December

6.6 Food Service Management in the State 
 
Under food service management, proper storage of food grains is a primary and important 
dimension, enabling farmers to preserve their produce safely even during adverse weather conditions. 
In recent years, with the strengthening of the state’s supply chain, digital systems have been adopted 
to ensure the swift execution of activities, thereby guaranteeing timely availability of food grains to 
the public. In Uttar Pradesh, a total of 234 warehouses (152 of the State Warehousing Corporation, 
48 of the Indian Warehousing Corporation and 34 of the Central Warehousing Corporation) were 
operational in 2017-18, which increased by 23.93% to 290 warehouses (182 of the State Warehousing 
Corporation, 48 of the Indian Warehousing Corporation, and 60 of the Central Warehousing 
Corporation) in 2024-25. The average storage capacity of warehouses in the state was 59.43 Lakh 
metric tons in 2017-18, which has risen by 14.49% to 68.04 Lakh metric tons in 2024-25. 
 
Under the National Agriculture Development Scheme, out of 103 approved rural warehouses 
with a capacity of 100 metric tons, construction of 88 has been completed while the rest are under 
progress; similarly, out of 24 approved rural warehouses with a capacity of 250 metric tons, 
construction of 6 has been completed and the remaining are still under construction. In addition, 
within the PCF, out of 11 approved rural warehouses aimed at creating a capacity of 11,800 metric 
tons, construction of 5 has been completed while the others are in progress. Under the world’s largest

6.8 Zero Hunger and Availability of Nutritious Food for All 
To achieve this goal by 2030, the state government is committed to ensuring safe, nutritious, and 
adequate food for all needy people, including women and children. For this purpose, the Government 
of Uttar Pradesh is effectively implementing the National Food Security Act, 2013 to provide food 
security to eligible families. At the same time, to improve agricultural productivity and enhance 
farmers’ income, the government is taking necessary steps to promote agricultural diversification 
through livestock rearing, dairy farming, poultry, fisheries, horticulture, aquaculture, and mushroom 
cultivation. 
According to the updated SDG India Index 2023-24 published by NITI Aayog, under 
Sustainable Development Goal-2 (Zero Hunger), indicator 2.1 “Coverage of beneficiaries under 
NFSA” recorded a national average of 99.01 percent, while Uttar Pradesh achieved 99.29 percent, 
thereby ranking 7th among Indian states. In this indicator, Andhra Pradesh, Bihar, Chhattisgarh, Goa, 
Haryana, Karnataka, Kerala, Maharashtra, Meghalaya, Punjab, Uttarakhand, and West Bengal 
attained 100 percent coverage and secured the top position. Notably, in the SDG India Index 202021 ranking, Uttar Pradesh had scored 41 under SDG-2 and was placed in the Aspirant category, 
whereas in 2023-24, the state improved by 9 points to reach a score of 50, thereby moving into the 
Performer category. 
Based on the NFHS-3 (2005-06), NFHS-4 (2015-16), and NFHS-5 (2019-21) surveys, NITI 
Aayog has published the National Multidimensional Poverty Index, which assesses poverty through 
key indicators of health, education, and living standards. Using these NFHS datasets, state-wise 
poverty estimates have also been prepared for the period 2013-14 to 2022-23 in terms of the 
Headcount Ratio. According to this assessment, multidimensional poverty in India declined from 
29.17% in 2013-14 to 11.28% in 2022-23, while in Uttar Pradesh it fell from 42.59% to 17.40% 
during the same period. Significantly, of the 24.82 Crore people who moved out of poverty in India, 
Uttar Pradesh accounted for the largest share with 5.94 Crore people. Improvements in food security 
and nutrition, sanitation, cooking fuel, access to drinking water and electricity in remote areas, 
housing availability, school education and attendance, as well as reductions in infant and maternal 
mortality, have all contributed to inclusive development and played a vital role in reducing 
multidimensional poverty in the state.

progress in reducing diarrhoea and other water-borne diseases, thereby improving public health. 
Preventing illness also lowers medical expenses, while the time earlier spent on arranging water can 
now be devoted to education, skill development, and income-generating activities. Clearly, the 
availability of clean water in rural areas contributes to poverty reduction and overall social welfare.

7.2 Strengthening Panchayats 
In recent years, the State Government has made positive efforts to provide greater autonomy 
and self-reliance to the three-tier Panchayat system- Gram Panchayat, Kshetra Panchayat, and Zila 
Panchayat. Panchayats are being empowered by involving them in village development works, 
ensuring financial autonomy/inclusion, and digitising the Panchayati system. The e-Gram Swaraj 
Portal and digital Panchayats have enhanced transparency and accountability in functioning. 
Panchayats now play a decisive role in planning and implementing schemes at the local level. Gram 
Panchayats are no longer merely nominal institutions; they are emerging as the “voice and hope” of 
rural development. 
7.2.1 Budgetary Framework 
The Panchayats of the State are being economically strengthened through budgetary 
arrangements made under the State Finance and the Central Finance. During the period from 2017-18 
to 2024-25, against the budgetary provision of Rs. 54,380.03 Crore under State Finance for 
Panchayati Raj institutions, Rs. 53,863.40 Crore was released and 100 percent expenditure was 
incurred. Similarly, under Central Finance, against the budgetary/released amount of Rs. 62,954.37 
Crore, 100 percent expenditure of Rs. 62,954.37 Crore was made. For the year 2025-26, a budgetary 
provision of Rs. 10,800 Crore has been made under State Finance and Rs. 7,797 Crore under Central 
Finance. 
The funds of the Fifth State Finance Commission are being utilised for works such as 
maintenance of government buildings, street lighting, elimination of open defecation, payment of 
electricity bills of public places, construction of Panchayat roads, solid and liquid waste management, 
and construction of boundaries at cremation grounds. From the funds of the Fifteenth Central Finance 
Commission, works are being carried out under tied and untied heads in areas such as sanitation, 
household waste management and treatment, faecal sludge/sewage management including plastic 
waste, availability of drinking water, rainwater harvesting and water recycling, along with activities 
Innovative Practices of the State Drinking Water and Sanitation Mission 
 One of the major challenges of the Jal Jeevan Mission is to ensure uninterrupted power supply for drinking 
water supply systems. In such remote areas of the State where conventional electricity is not available, rural 
drinking water supply projects are being operated through renewable solar energy. 
 As of January 2026, out of 40,955 drinking water supply projects, 33,157 projects are presently solar-based, 
with a solar capacity of about 900 megawatts. These solar energy-based projects will saturate a total of 67,013 
villages, thereby benefitting a population of 13.30 Crore. 
 Solar energy has facilitated timely completion of projects, resulting in substantial savings in operating costs 
and a significant reduction in carbon footprint. Taking into account a 2% annual cost escalation over 30 years, 
the estimated savings in operating costs is about Rs. 37,395 Crore. 
 In addition, the annual reduction in CO₂ emissions is estimated at 13 Lakh metric tons, which is equivalent 
to 13 Lakh carbon credits. This could generate revenue of about 78 million US dollars over 30 years. 
 Under the Mission, at the Panchayat level, by January 2026, 7.56 Lakh youths have been trained as 
electricians, masons, pump operators, plumbers, fitters, and motor mechanics, thereby making them skilled. 
Along with this, a total of 5.51 Lakh women has been trained to test water quality through field test kits. 
 The State Drinking Water and Sanitation Mission have conducted Stop Diarrhoea Campaigns, under which 
the Mission has carried out awareness activities at district, block, and village levels through initiatives such 
as Know Your Water and campaigns for identification and repair of water leakages.

7.2.2 National Gram Swaraj Abhiyan 
 The National Gram Swaraj Abhiyan scheme has been implemented since 2018-19 with the 
objective of enhancing the capacity and effectiveness of Panchayats and Gram Sabhas and 
strengthening them. For the financial year 2025-26, a budgetary provision of Rs. 373.04 Crore (Rs. 
223.82 Crore as Central share and Rs. 149.21 Crore as State share) has been made, against which an 
annual action plan of Rs. 320.11 Crore has been approved at the level of the Ministry of Panchayati 
Raj, Government of India. 
7.2.3 Swachh Bharat Mission (Rural) 
The Swachh Bharat Mission has been operational in the State since 2014, establishing 
cleanliness as a mission and undertaking commendable work to create awareness in society about 
freedom from open defecation. In the first phase of the Mission (2014-19), all Gram Panchayats of 
the State were declared Open Defecation Free (ODF). Subsequently, from April 2020, the second 
phase (2020-27) was launched with the objective of sustaining villages as ODF and improving the 
sanitation situation in rural areas through solid and liquid waste management, thereby transforming 
them into ODF Plus villages. 
From financial year 2017-18 to 2025-26 (up to 31.01.2026), construction of 2.74 Lakh 
individual toilets, 58,591 community toilets, 94,141 ODF Plus model villages, 103 declared plastic 
management units, and 115 functional biogas plants under the Gobardhan scheme has been 
completed. With the objective of increasing the sources of income of Gram Panchayats and 
strengthening service delivery, Panchayat Assistants working in Panchayats are being trained for 
electricity bill collection, Aadhaar registration, and as banking agents. 
Key Accomplishments under the National Gram Swaraj Abhiyan, 2025 26 
Training of 3,08,253 Panchayat representatives, functionaries, and officers has been completed. 
With 92 percent progress in the authentication of trainees, the Department has been holding the first 
position at the national level for the past four months. 
Against the construction units sanctioned under the scheme, work on 393 units (296 Common 
Service Centres, 54 Panchayat Bhawans, and 43 PLCs) has been completed. 
Under the scheme, 380 participants (Gram Panchayat/Block level representatives and functionaries) 
have been sent on exposure visits outside the State to Telangana, Maharashtra, Jharkhand, Tripura, 
and Odisha. 
Two hundred district and block level representatives, functionaries, and officers have been trained 
through prestigious institutions such as IIM Lucknow and IIT Kanpur. 
Memorandums of Understanding have been signed with six universities/educational institutions to 
provide handholding support to 750 Gram Panchayats of the State for preparation of plans. 
Internal exposure visits of more than 1,025 participants have been conducted. 
For qualitative conduct of training work in all divisions of the country, District Panchayat Resource 
Centres have been expanded under the chairmanship of the Divisional Commissioner.

centre of agriculture and culture but also as a new symbol of India’s industrial strength. The State 
aims to become a one-trillion-dollar economy in the coming years and to play a leading role in India’s 
industrial progress. In this journey, production technology and innovation hold a crucial role in 
enhancing the value of primary sector products, thereby driving employment generation and 
economic growth while significantly improving the income and living standards of the people. 
Uttar Pradesh, once known primarily as an agrarian State, is today reaching new heights of 
industrial development. Policies framed by the State Government to promote investment such as One 
District One Product (ODOP), the development of industrial corridors, and the establishment of land 
banks have attracted entrepreneurs. Cities like Noida, Ghaziabad, Kanpur, Lucknow, and Varanasi 
have emerged as thriving industrial hubs, witnessing rapid investment in sectors such as information 
technology, electronics, textiles, and food processing. Institutions like Invest UP and the Uttar

8.3 Index of Industrial Production (IIP) 
Index of Industrial Production (IIP) is an important indicator for measuring the progress of 
a country’s industrial sector, providing valuable insights for economic analysis, policy formulation, 
and strategic planning. It measures changes in the volume of production in the industrial sector over 
a specified period. The IIP covers manufacturing, mining, and electricity generation, reflecting the 
diverse segments of the industrial landscape. 
 In the state’s Index of Industrial Production, a progressive increase has been observed. In 
the financial year 2023-24, the annual industrial 
production index for the manufacturing sector

industrial production index for the electricity 
sector was 162.8 in the previous year, which

industrial index recorded a growth rate of 2.6 
percent over the previous year, reflecting the 
broad-based advancement of industrial progress (Figure 8.5).

months after the reference month. An analysis of the monthly index reveals that, compared to 
November 2024, the indices for manufacturing, electricity, and the general monthly index all 
registered increases in November 2025 (Figure 8.5 a). This progress reflects the strong position of 
the economy.

Authority (BIDA) is a flagship initiative of the 
Government of Uttar Pradesh, designed to 
transform the Bundelkhand region into a major 
industrial and economic hub, modelled on Noida. 
Its objectives include promoting industrial 
development, attracting investment, enhancing 
skills, and generating local employment across the 
region. For the comprehensive development of

PM MITRA (Prime Minister Mega Integrated Textile Region and 
Apparel) Park 
The establishment of the PM MITRA (Prime Minister Mega Integrated Textile 
Region and Apparel) Park in Uttar Pradesh is a major step towards promoting the 
textile industry and creating an industrial ecosystem. Being developed on over 1,000 
acres along the Lucknow-Hardoi border, the park will integrate facilities for yarn 
production, fabric manufacturing, weaving, and apparel making at one location. It is 
expected to attract investment of over Rs. 10,000 Crore and generate more than 1 
Lakh direct and 2 Lakh indirect jobs, thereby strengthening the state’s textile sector 
at a global level. Against the total project cost of Rs. 409.39 Crore, Rs. 206.95 Crore 
has already been released, of which Rs. 25.91 Crore has been utilized. For external 
infrastructure of the park, such as road connectivity, 77 percent physical progress has 
been achieved in the first phase. In the second phase, land acquisition proceedings are 
underway for the construction of a 14.28 km greenfield four-lane road from Raitha 
underpass to the park gate. Works related to boundary wall, gate complex, office, 
construction of a 132 KV sub-station for power supply within the park premises, and 
water supply are in progress

8.6.1 Establishment and Growth of Start-ups in Uttar Pradesh 
To encourage the start-up culture in the state and to establish a world-class start-up 
ecosystem by developing strong infrastructure and providing a favourable environment, the 
Government of Uttar Pradesh promulgated the Start-up Policy, 2020. In view of the rapid growth in 
the start-up sector and the changes in the ecosystem in recent years, the policy was reviewed and 
subsequently revised in 2022 to further promote entrepreneurship and innovation among youth. At 
present, the state has 19,042 start-ups, along with 76 recognized incubators and 7 Centres of 
excellence in fields such as Artificial Intelligence, MedTech, drones, and additive engineering. As a 
result of the continuous efforts of the state government, Uttar Pradesh has been included in the ‘Top 
Performer’ Category A-1 in the fifth edition of the State Start-up Ecosystem Ranking published by 
the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT), Government of India, in 
January 2026. 
8.6.2 Special Economic Zones (SEZs) in Uttar Pradesh 
In Uttar Pradesh, 31 Special Economic Zones (SEZs) have been approved, providing modern 
office spaces ready for use. The state has established itself as a data centre and semiconductor hub in 
North India, with leading companies such as Yotta, STT Global, and Web Werks already operating 
here. The state government has announced a Semiconductor Park near Jewar International Airport, 
with connectivity to the Yamuna Expressway Industrial Development Authority (YEIDA) multimodal logistics park and the Rapid Rail Transit System. In addition, the YEIDA region hosts a 250acre Electronic Park, a Data Centre Park, and other electronic manufacturing clusters. To meet the 
requirements of various sectors such as IT/ITeS, textiles, handicrafts, and non-conventional energy, 
the Government of Uttar Pradesh has approved 31 SEZs. Of these, approximately 74 percent are 
IT/ITeS, 20 percent are multi-product, 3 percent are textiles/handicrafts, and 3 percent are nonconventional energy.

Investors’ Summit and Ground Breaking Ceremony 
To attract global investment, the Government organizes Global Investors’ Summits and 
Ground Breaking Ceremonies from time to time. So far, four Ground Breaking Ceremonies have 
been held in the state, with the fourth organized in February 2024. The total proposed capital 
investment in the state has now reached approximately Rs. 50 Lakh Crore, which is expected to 
generate nearly 10 Lakh employment opportunities. 
So far, four groundbreaking ceremonies have been successfully conducted, through which 
more than 8,300 projects have reached the stage of commercial operations, while over 8,100 projects 
are under implementation. The highest number of projects reaching commercial operations are in 
Gautam Buddha Nagar (35.3%), followed by Lucknow (7.28%), Mathura (4.07%), Jhansi (3.47%), 
Bareilly (3.44%), and Moradabad (3.17%). At the regional level, 16.40% of projects are operational 
in Purvanchal, 15.29% in Madhyanchal, 4.58% in Bundelkhand, and 63.72% in Paschimanchal. 
8.6.3 Key Industrial Policies of Uttar Pradesh 
These policies of the Government of Uttar Pradesh have been formulated to attract 
investment in industry, technology, energy, and other sectors, to generate employment, and to make 
the state competitive at both the national and global levels. The major policies promulgated by the 
state government include: 
Through the Semiconductor Policy-2024, the State Government aims to establish Uttar 
Pradesh as a preferred destination for the semiconductor industry by creating world-class 
infrastructure facilities and a conducive policy environment, thereby positioning the state as a 
significant hub for semiconductor manufacturing. Uttar Pradesh is the fourth state in the country to 
initiate dedicated provisions for semiconductor units. 
The objective of the Uttar Pradesh Green Hydrogen Policy-2024 is to promote 
decarbonization and prioritize the state’s contribution to India’s climate goals, while simultaneously 
fostering development and employment within the state. Through this policy, investment will be 
encouraged in green hydrogen/ammonia production, market creation, demand aggregation, and the 
establishment of a favourable ecosystem in the state. 
 
World Economic Forum 
In January 2026, the Government of Uttar Pradesh participated in the World Economic Forum held 
in Davos, Switzerland, where significant agreements were signed. With Memorandums of Understanding 
worth Rs. 2,94,255 Crore, Uttar Pradesh has demonstrated strong investment potential in emerging sectors 
such as clean energy, digital infrastructure, artificial intelligence, and defence manufacturing. Partnerships 
include leading international companies such as Ever Sunshine Capital Group, Inox GFL, Arna Pharma, and 
Yeoman, among others. These collaborations align with the state’s long-term vision of sustainable 
development, technology-enabled governance, large-scale employment generation, and enhanced global 
competitiveness. This initiative will pave the way for new partnerships in the future and accelerate the state’s 
economic progress and global integration.

Integrated Manufacturing and Logistics Cluster (IMLC) 
In the state, Integrated Manufacturing and Logistics Clusters (IMLCs) are being developed along 
the expressways as major industrial hubs. Their primary objective is to bring industries, manufacturing units, 
and logistics services together at one location, thereby making production and supply chains more efficient, 
faster, and cost-effective. Under IMLC, across 26 districts namely Unnao, Hardoi, Banda, Shahjahanpur,

clusters into a modern, multimodal, and technology-based logistics industry ecosystem, thereby promoting 
industrial growth, exports, and employment generation at the local level in the state.

strength of public health. Health is directly linked not only to individual well-being but also to the

participate in education, production, labour, and social activities, thereby accelerating economic 
development. Therefore, it would be entirely 
appropriate to call health the foundation of economic 
progress.

9.8 (I) Ayushman Bharat- Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana and 
Mukhyamantri Jan Arogya Abhiyan 
Across the entire state, the Ayushman Bharat-Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana is being 
operated in trust mode by the Department of Medical, Health, and Family Welfare, and its 
implementation is carried out through the State Agency for Comprehensive Health and Integrated 
Services (SACHI). This scheme provides health security to 61.7 Lakh families listed under the 
National Food Security Act, all families of the Buksa tribe, and all senior citizens aged 70 years and 
above. Families covered under the Ayushman Bharat scheme are provided free treatment facilities. 
Under the scheme, eligible families can avail completely cashless and paperless treatment in 
listed government and private hospitals within the state and in other states where the scheme is 
implemented. All identified beneficiaries are issued an “Ayushman Card,” through which they can 
access treatment packages/procedures for more than 1,900 diseases, including cancer, brain tumor, 
heart disease, cataract, kidney disease, and knee replacement. 
 
9.8 (II) Mukhyamantri Jan Arogya Yojana 
The Government of Uttar Pradesh launched the Mukhyamantri Jan Arogya Yojana in 2019 
to provide health security to families not covered under the Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana. At 
present, the scheme covers 8.43 Lakh families excluded from the SECC 2011 list, 40.79 Lakh 
Antyodaya ration cardholder families, 11.65 Lakh families registered with the Uttar Pradesh Building 
and Other Construction Workers Welfare Board, and families of accredited journalists registered 
with the Department of Information and Public Relations. 
Achievements 
By December 2025, a total of 1.93 Crore families has been covered under both schemes in Uttar 
Pradesh, with the total number of beneficiaries reaching 9.15 Crore. From the inception of the 
scheme up to December 2025, 5.42 Crore Ayushman Cards have been issued to beneficiaries, 
which is the highest in the country. Among the eligible families, 87.08% have at least one member 
with a card. By December 2025, 83.11 Lakh free treatments have been provided, amounting to an 
expenditure of Rs. 13,615 Crore. As of December 2025, a total of 6,257 hospitals (2,948 
government and 3,309 private) has been empanelled under the scheme, which is also the highest 
in the country.

increased and treatment activities have been consistently strengthened. Compared to 36 labouratories in 29 
districts in the year 2017, by the year 2025, advanced diagnostic facilities for dengue have been made 
available with 89 labouratories operational in all districts of the state. At present, 86 sentinel labouratories 
and three apex labouratories are functional in the state. 
• Due to continuous improvement in rapid disease diagnosis and treatment facilities, the mortality rate of 
dengue disease in the year 2025 has decreased by 96.4 percent compared to the year 2017. 
• In the year 2017, a total of 32,342 malaria patients were reported, whereas in the year 2025, a total of 
14,688 malaria patients were reported. Thus, there has been a 55 percent reduction in the total number of 
malaria patients. 
• Compared to a total of 46.69 lakh malaria tests conducted in the year 2017, 1.54 Crore malaria tests were 
conducted in the state in the year 2025, resulting in a 229 percent increase in the number of malaria tests.

Rail Transport 
The Indian Railways system plays a vital role in the transportation framework of the region. 
In Uttar Pradesh, the railway infrastructure not only connects the state internally but also links it 
efficiently with other parts of the country. The rail network contributes significantly to the state’s 
economic growth by facilitating the transport of agricultural produce, industrial goods, and raw 
materials. At the same time, it serves as a lifeline for millions of passengers, providing a reliable, 
affordable, and extensive mode of transport. In the financial year 2017-18, the gross value added 
from the railway sector at current prices was Rs. 20.37 thousand Crore. Growing at a compound 
annual growth rate of 9.62 percent, it has reached Rs. 38.74 thousand Crore according to the quick 
estimates of 2024-25. As per these estimates, the sector accounts for 1.28 percent of the state’s Gross 
State Value Added. Uttar Pradesh has the largest railway route length in India, with 8,821 kilometres, 
representing about 12.50 percent of the country’s total rail network.

Water Transport 
The first inland waterway in Uttar Pradesh is National Waterway‑1, which runs along the 
Ganga and Hooghly rivers from Haldia in West Bengal to Prayagraj in Uttar Pradesh. Of its total 
navigable length, 425 km (about 26 percent of the catchment area) lies within Uttar Pradesh, 
connecting major export centres such as Varanasi and Prayagraj with Haldia Port. India’s first 
multimodal terminal has been established at Varanasi, equipped with container cargo‑handling 
capacity. This waterway links North India with Eastern and Northeastern India, Bangladesh, 
Myanmar, and other South Asian countries through Haldia Port and Kolkata. Under terminal 
expansion plans, freight village projects are being developed at Ramnagar (Varanasi), 
Chandauli, and Mirzapur, along with an intermodal terminal at Ghazipur. At the intermodal 
terminal, products transported by road will be exported via water transport. 
With the objective of promoting water transport and water tourism in the State, the process 
of establishing the Uttar Pradesh Inland Waterways Authority on the lines of the Inland Waterways 
Authority of India is underway. It is noteworthy that out of the 111 National Waterways declared by 
the Government of India, 11 waterways are located in Uttar Pradesh, which are based on the rivers 
Ganga, Gandak, Assi, Chambal, Ghaghra, Gomti, Tons, Varuna, Karmanasha, and Yamuna.

Policies Implemented in the State for Energy Conservation 
Uttar Pradesh Solar Energy Policy - 2022 
Under the Uttar Pradesh Solar Energy Policy 2022, a target of 22,000 MW solar capacity has been set for 
the next five years. This includes 6,000 MW from rooftop plants, 14,000 MW from utility scale/solar parks, 
and 2,000 MW through the PM KUSUM scheme. Under the policy, 11.27 Lakh households will be covered 
with rooftop plants and provided with state subsidies. Ayodhya will be developed as a model solar city, 
while 16 municipal corporations and Noida will be developed as solar cities. The policy also includes 
concessional leasing of public and private land, skill development for 30,000 youth, promotion of battery 
storage, and transmission support in Bundelkhand and Purvanchal. In addition, grid connected rooftop 
projects are being encouraged through net metering arrangements with subsidies from both the central and 
state governments. 
Uttar Pradesh Bio Energy Policy-2022 
The objective of this policy is to promote bio energy production from agriculture, livestock, sugar mills, and 
municipal waste. The policy provides for subsidies up to Rs. 20 Crore for compressed biogas, bio coal, and 
bio diesel plants, exemption from electricity duty and stamp duty for 10 years, and an additional 30% subsidy 
for aggregators. For projects with investment exceeding Rs. 50 Crore, the state government will also 
construct a 5 km road from the plant to the main route. At present, the production capacity of compressed 
biogas (CBG) plants established in the state is 213 tons per day, which is driving investment, employment, 
and sustainable development. A total of 36 CBG plants have been set up in the state, placing it first in the 
country. The first biogas based CBG plant in Gorakhpur district has been established by Indian Oil 
Corporation Limited (IOCL). 
Uttar Pradesh Green Hydrogen Policy - 2024 
The objective of this policy is to promote solar-energy-based green hydrogen/ammonia production, thereby 
contributing to investment, employment, and climate goals. It includes provisions such as 30-40% capital 
subsidy, land concessions, exemption from stamp duty, land allocation for captive solar plants, special 
concessions in power supply, and categorization of environmental clearance under the white category. This 
policy will create a favourable ecosystem for green hydrogen industries in the state. Under this, approval 
has been granted for the establishment of two Centers of Excellence in the state. In addition, Memorandums 
of Understanding (MoUs) have been signed with technical institutions IIT Kanpur, IIT Delhi, and the 
Institute of Solar Energy for technical collaboration in renewable energy production.

Uttar Pradesh is becoming the country’s leading tourism destination through its cultural 
heritage and policy. In 2024, 64.91 Crore tourists arrived, and in 2025, including the Maha

Uttar Pradesh has overtaken Tamil Nadu to secure first place in tourist arrivals nationwide. 
In domestic tourism, the state’s share was 16.2% in 2021 (ranked second), which increased 
to 18.4% in 2022, 19.1% in 2023, and 21.9% in 2024, making it the top state in the country.

An innovative eco-tourism initiative has been introduced, integrating biodiversity 
conservation with homestays and handicrafts to foster local development, with 49 projects 
underway. On National Tourism Day 2025, the theme “Tourism for Inclusive Development”
highlighted employment generation and regional prosperity. 
At Prayagraj Maha Kumbh 2025, 66.30 Crore pilgrims/tourists attended, which is 175.7% 
higher compared to Kumbh 2019. This figure represents the highest-ever tourist presence at 
a single cultural event globally.
