Operating heritage buildings under adaptive re-use 
Six historic forts and heritage sites of the state Chhatar Manzil (Lucknow), Chunar Fort (Mirzapur), 
Barua Sagar Fort (Jhansi), Kothi Roshan-ud-Daula (Lucknow), Jal Mahal (Barsana), and Shukla 
Talab (Kanpur) have been made available to private investors on a 90-year lease for development 
and operation under Public-Private Partnership (PPP), as part of adaptive re-use initiatives. 
These monuments, after being de-notified by the State Archaeology Department, have been 
transferred to the Tourism Department, where they can be utilized under the private participation 
model for activities such as heritage hotels, resort museums, MICE (Meetings, Incentives, 
Conferences, Exhibitions), and other cultural-tourism services. This initiative is also giving shape 
to the concept of food circuits and is leading to the development of world-class heritage hotels.

11.3 Special Focus on 12 Thematic Areas for Tourism Growth in 
Uttar Pradesh 
 
The concept is to identify and develop thematic regions across the state according to diverse 
tourism themes, while promoting tourism-related employment. 
1. Heritage, Art and Culture: Development of tourism sites while preserving the culture and 
heritage of Uttar Pradesh. Identification of major sites including Bundelkhand, listing for 
UNESCO and other heritage programs, and promotion of international events (Kumbh, Yoga, 
Art, Buddhist Conclave, etc.). 
Uttar Pradesh Tourism Policy 
This policy presents a roadmap to make the state an attractive tourism destination by linking tourism 
with investment, employment, cultural preservation, and global competitiveness. Its aim is to 
provide the best tourism experience, attract investment, and elevate the industry globally. Based on 
principles of information, welcome, convenience, safety, cleanliness, infrastructure, and 
cooperation, the policy ensures financial assistance, subsidies, and grants. Granting industry status 
to registered star hotels/resorts and defined projects, along with State Tourism Awards for 
excellence, are key features. Through special tourism sites and thematic regions, the policy promotes 
investment, employment, and holistic tourist experiences. Under rural tourism, 85 homestay/farm 
stay units and 155 tour operators have been registered. For cultural preservation, Rs. 30 Lakh has 
been granted to six individuals/groups for art, music, crafts, folk dance, and cuisine, while nine 
studies in tourism/hospitality have been approved with grants of Rs. 85 Lakh. 
The Uttar Pradesh Bed and Breakfast and Homestay Policy- 2025 has been promulgated 
with the objective of improving service standards and diversifying accommodation 
options.

2. Spiritual and Religious Tourism: Quality facilities at pilgrimage sites in the spirit of Atithi 
Devo Bhava. Promotion of Ramayana, Buddhist, Krishna, and Sufi circuits, and interlinking of 
national and international journeys. 
3. Eco, Nature and Wildlife: Promotion of eco-tourism along with wildlife conservation and 
environmental balance. Sustainable development of sanctuaries and natural resources. 
4. Wellness and Medical Tourism: Development of yoga, Ayurveda, and health-promoting sites 
such as Sarnath, Shravasti, Kapilvastu, Varanasi, and Mathura with world-class units.

5. Meetings, Conferences and Exhibitions: Modern convention Centres in Agra and Ghaziabad. 
Emphasis on national and international meetings, exhibitions, and mega events. 
6. Adventure Tourism: Promotion of activities such as camping, trekking, ziplining, rock 
climbing, and cave exploration. Formation of an Adventure Tourism Board. Development of sites 
in Bundelkhand, Sonbhadra, Chitrakoot, Varanasi, etc. 
7. Water-based Tourism: Cruises, houseboats, floating restaurants in Varanasi and Chitrakoot. 
Development of jetties, marinas, and other water-based facilities. 
8. Agri-Tourism: Guided tours, knowledge sessions, animal rides, and local cuisine based on 
agricultural activities. 
9. Cuisine Tourism: Annual programs on diverse local cuisines of districts. Promotion of 
innovation and documentation in culinary traditions. 
10. Rural/Tribal Tourism: Entrepreneurship and employment generation in rural and tribal areas. 
Establishment of such tourism Centres near Agra, Varanasi, Lucknow, Ayodhya, and Prayagraj. 
11. Youth Tourism: Preservation of culture and heritage through Youth Tourism Clubs. Connecting 
youth with responsible and sustainable tourism. 
12. Wedding Destination Tourism: Grand wedding events in palatial and heritage properties. 
Online listing and promotion with the support of wedding planners and event management.

 Flag Hoisting at Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Temple and Deepotsav in Ayodhya 
In Ayodhya, on November 25, 2025, a grand saffron-coloured triangular flag measuring 22 feet 
in length and 11 feet in width was hoisted atop the newly constructed Shri Ram Janmabhoomi 
Temple’s 161-foot-high spire. This Dharma flag bears the radiant Sun, the symbol ‘Om,’ and the 
Kovidar tree, representing Lord Ram’s brilliance, valor, sacrifice, and devotion, as well as dignity, 
unity, and the ideals of Ram Rajya. Earlier, on January 22, 2025, the consecration of the idol of Ram 
Lalla was performed in the newly built temple, and with the flag hoisting on November 25, 2025, 
Ayodhya, the city of Maryada Purushottam Shri Ram, has emerged as a major centre of faith. The

limitless possibilities in the tourism sector, creating employment, boosting the local economy, and

development. In the year 2025 (from January to December), 29.96 Crore tourists visited Ayodhya 
Dham, marking 1.8 times increase compared to 16.44 Crore tourists in 2024, setting a new benchmark 
in the State.

celebration is proclaimed on the basis of mythological, spiritual, and astrological perspectives. In 
accordance with astronomical phenomena, the tradition of spontaneously organizing the Kumbh 
Mela every 12 years continues at the Triveni Sangam in Prayagraj, on the banks of the Ganga in 
Haridwar, on the banks of the Shipra in Ujjain, and on the banks of the Godavari in Nashik. Thus, in 
the year 2025, the 43-day Prayagraj Mahakumbh 
has been organized.

ascetics that has nurtured the five elements,

Sangam of the Ganga, Yamuna, and Saraswati, 
whose supremely sacred waters are venerated as 
liberating. The organization of Prayagraj 
Mahakumbh 2025 has not only succeeded in 
firmly establishing India’s cultural diversity and 
spiritual energy on the world tourism map, but 
has also comprehensively showcased the unique religious tourism potential of Uttar Pradesh. 
Notably, the Kumbh, being the grand festival of 
the vast congregation of humanity, is also a 
symbol of peace, goodwill, harmony, and cultural 
unity on the global stage, where people bathe 
together without any discrimination to earn merit.

has recognized the Kumbh as an ‘Intangible

2025 depicts the Amrit Kalash along with three

11.9 International Recognition of Indian Theatrical Art 
In Uttar Pradesh, the two-year diploma course in theatrical art conducted by Bharatendu 
Natya Academy is being granted postgraduate recognition under Bhatkhande Sanskriti University, 
Lucknow. The objective of the Academy is to train trainees interested in theatre in various aspects of 
theatrical art through the two-year course, thereby promoting the culture of the nation and the state 
and providing employment opportunities. In the year 2024-25, the Academy provided training to 
students in September 2024 by Australia’s renowned director Prof. Peter Cook. In 2023, the State 
Government reorganized the Rang Mandal and selected 5 Rang Mandal heads and 19 artists in 5 
categories.

11.11 Branding of the State’s Rich Heritage and Tourist

Cinema is a powerful medium for presenting social and cultural changes through the screen, 
which has influenced public culture by leaving its imprint on people’s thoughts, attitudes, and 
behaviour. Uttar Pradesh, being rich in religious, spiritual, historical, and cultural heritage, is a state 
with immense potential for tourism. Here, films are not merely a means of entertainment but also a 
strong medium for social awareness, cultural promotion, and employment generation. In Uttar 
Pradesh, Film Bandhu has been constituted and the Film Development Council established, through

 For the effective implementation of the state’s film policy and in view of the possibilities of

and picturesque tourist destinations and, by attracting tourists, encouraging the production of regional 
films.

12.5.5 Digitization of Higher Education and Academic Infrastructure 
Digital transformation has emerged as a key driver of higher education reforms. Integrated 
academic and administrative platforms have enhanced transparency, reduced process time, and 
improved service delivery. 
State-level digital libraries, online content creation, digital academic records, and paperless 
administrative processes have expanded access to learning resources and strengthened governance 
efficiency. Integration with national digital credential systems has further reinforced the credibility, 
portability, and verification of academic qualifications. 
To ensure transparency in the affiliation process of universities and colleges, an online 
system has been made operational. In the academic session 2025-26, the portal Samarth is being 
effectively implemented across all state and private universities, under which all admission processes 
this year were conducted through Samarth. 
To facilitate the application of digital technology, the state government has provided mobile 
phones/tablets to students of higher education institutions. Most government colleges have been 
equipped with e-facility services and smart classrooms, and libraries have been furnished with 
pre-loaded tablets. 
At the directorate level, an e-content studio has been established to make teaching 
technology more accessible and meaningful, through which e-content recording is being carried out. 
A digital library of higher education has been set up, containing more than 86,000 e-contents across 
239 subjects. 
Higher education institutions in the state have begun using national digital platforms such as 
SWAYAM, Virtual Labs, I‑STEM, KAPILA, Institution Innovation Council, and Open Network 
Operating System. Steps have also been taken to implement DOI for the digitization of academic 
publications, enabling research conducted in the state to reach the international community and 
increasing their citations. 
12.5.6 Internationalization and Global Engagement 
A total of 288 international MoUs have been signed by universities in the state, of which the 
highest number 33 MoUs are with the United States, 21 with Nepal, and 19 with Russia. Through 
the various academic and research activities organized under these MoUs, 97,197 students and 259 
faculty members have benefitted. Institutional partnerships, joint programs, collaborative research 
initiatives, and global linkages contribute to improvements in academic standards, faculty 
development, and student outcomes.

State’s Educational Institutions 
 
 Under the guidelines of the University Grants Commission, the National Assessment and 
Accreditation Council (NAAC) evaluates the quality of government/ private universities and higher 
education institutions across the country on various parameters and provides grading. Uttar Pradesh 
has recorded remarkable progress in the field of quality assurance and accreditation. The number of

accreditation grades reflects enhancements in governance systems, infrastructure, and academic 
processes. The NAAC accreditation status of various educational institutions in the state is presented

Participation of the state’s institutions in the National Institutional Ranking Framework

improve the quality of higher education, a State Quality Assurance Cell has been established. By the 
year 2030, mandatory participation of all higher education institutions in NIRF will be ensured, and 
a special strategy focused on data-driven guidance, capacity building, and institutional performance 
improvement will be adopted to place at least 10 colleges among the top 200 ranks.

Major Efforts for Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities 
▪
Accessible India Campaign- To promote self‑reliance among persons with disabilities, physical environment, 
transport, and communication systems are being developed. In Phase‑1, out of 139 buildings in 6 districts, 98 have 
been made disability‑friendly; in Phase‑2, out of 68 buildings in Lucknow, 23 have been made accessible; and in 
Phase‑3, action is being taken to make 508 buildings in 10 districts convenient for persons with disabilities. 
▪
Free Bus Travel Facility- Since 21 June 2019, free travel facility has been provided in State Transport Corporation 
buses for persons with disabilities. In the year 2024-25, an expenditure of Rs. 40 Crore was incurred to benefit 23.84 
Lakh persons with disabilities through this facility. 
▪
Unique Disability Identity Certificate- On the basis of the Disability Certificate, Unique Identity Cards (UDID 
Cards) are being issued. In the state, as of January 2026, out of a total of 19.74 Lakh registered on the UDID portal, 
16.19 Lakh (82.02%) cards have been issued. In state services, 4% reservation and in educational institutions, 5% 
reservation is being provided. 
▪
Special Schools- The State Government is operating Prayas (Government High School for physically disabled 
children), Sanket (Government Junior High School for speech and hearing-impaired children), Mamta (Government 
School for mentally challenged boys/girls), and Sparsh (Government School for visually impaired children). All 16 
special schools have been granted ISO 9001:2015 certification. At present, 1,488 students are studying in these schools 
equipped with smart classes. Smart classes have been arranged in these schools with the objective of providing quality 
education. 
▪
Integrated Special Schools- For the purpose of inclusive education of persons with disabilities, integrated special 
schools are presently being operated in 07 districts for visually impaired, hearing impaired, and orthopedically 
impaired boys/girls to study along with general students from classes 6 to 12, in which 529 students are enrolled. 
Among these, the new schools in Ballia and Maharajganj have been started in the year 2025-26. In addition, 
proceedings are underway for the operation of integrated special secondary schools in 5 districts - Ghaziabad, 
Mirzapur, Etah, Pratapgarh, and Bulandshahr, and an integrated special secondary school is under construction in

14. Labour & Employment 
 The foundation of any nation’s socio-economic development rests on its labour force and 
the employment system that guides it. The term “labour force” refers to the working population that 
is capable of performing work and is willing to actively contribute to production, services, and 
developmental activities through their effort, knowledge, and skills. Employment services, on the 
other hand, refer to the process of proper planning, training, and providing jobs to the labour force in 
accordance with their qualifications, interests, and abilities. This includes mechanisms such as 
employment exchanges, employment departments, skill development programs, and career 
counselling services. 
In the present era, rapid technological advancement, industrialization, and the expansion of 
the services sector have significantly increased the demand for skill-based employment. Therefore, 
it is essential to train the labour force in modern technologies. With this objective, the government is 
promoting initiatives such as the Skill Development Mission, apprenticeship programs, and start-ups. 
Uttar Pradesh, being the largest consumer and labour market in the country, has the potential to 
achieve new heights of economic growth if its labour force is provided with proper employment 
services, training, and opportunities. Ensuring fair participation of citizens in resources, employment, 
and services according to their qualifications is the core objective of the Uttar Pradesh government 
as a welfare state. According to Census 2011, Uttar Pradesh was the most populous state in the 
country with a population of 19.98 Crore. Based on updated demographic projections, the state’s 
population is estimated to reach 24.05 Crore on March 1, 2025.

promotion of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs), and the creation of employment 
opportunities for the unemployed in both rural and urban areas.

14.3.3 Key Employment Generation Programmes 
To provide employment opportunities, an Employment Web Portal has been developed in 
the state, which is also known as Rojgar Sangam. Its objective is to connect unemployed youth of 
the state with jobs in both the government and private sectors. Through this portal, youth can register 
and apply online for jobs according to their qualifications, as well as access information about job 
fairs and skill development programs. This web portal not only makes a greater number of 
employment opportunities accessible to unemployed candidates, but also enables employers to find 
qualified and trained candidates. As of December 31, 2025, the number of registered job-seeking 
candidates on the Employment Portal was 44.83 Lakh, while the number of registered and verified 
employers was 13,755.

15. Policies of the State Government 
Uttar Pradesh, owing to its vast and diverse demographic structure, holds a position of 
paramount importance in the country. The future of its economic, social, and cultural development 
depends on policies rooted in an inclusive vision and supported by effective implementation. Over 
the past eight years, the state government has announced and redefined 34 policies with long-term 
strategy and confidence across different sectors of the economy. These policies have particularly 
attracted investors, propelling the state forward toward becoming a trillion-dollar economy and 
achieving the vision of Viksit Uttar Pradesh 2047. As one of the fastest-growing economies in the 
country, Uttar Pradesh has prioritized the rapid development of infrastructure facilities. 
Consequently, the business environment has witnessed unprecedented improvement, and the state is 
steadily emerging as a hub of investment and industrial progress. This chapter presents a concise 
outline of these policies and a brief analysis of their economic impact, which clearly highlights the 
overall economic advancement of Uttar Pradesh. More details about these policies are available on 
the official website: https://invest.up.gov.in/policies/. 
The Government of Uttar Pradesh has announced and redefined 34 policies across various 
sectors, along with the upcoming Sustainable Aviation Fuel Manufacturing Promotion 
Policy 2025. 
Owing to the positive impact of these policies implemented in the state, Uttar Pradesh has so 
far attracted investments worth Rs. 50 Lakh Crore, with major investors including Varun 
Beverages, Honda Motors, Samsung, and Amba Shakti. 
Uttar Pradesh has become India’s largest exporter of consumer electronics. The industrial 
areas developed in Sector 24 of the Yamuna Expressway Authority and in Ecotech VI and 
VII of Greater Noida have firmly established the state as a leading electronics hub.

1. Policies related to the Agriculture and Food Processing 
Sector 
The Government of Uttar Pradesh has recognized agriculture and food processing as the 
foundation of the state’s economy and rural development, and has accordingly introduced several 
visionary policies in this sector. The objective of these policies is to enhance farmers’ income, 
promote value addition in agricultural production, ensure food security, and position the state as a 
leading hub for the food processing industry. Key policies in this domain include the Food Processing 
Industry Policy 2023, Dairy Farm and Product Development Policy 2022, Poultry Development 
Policy 2022, and the Agricultural Export Promotion Policy. 
Uttar Pradesh Food Processing Industry Policy, 2023 
The Uttar Pradesh Food Processing Industry Policy, 2023 aims to promote the rapid 
development of food processing industries and related infrastructure across the state. The 
policy strengthens both potential and existing entrepreneurs by offering financial incentives, 
concessions in land use, exemptions on stamp duty, subsidies for solar energy, export 
incentives, and support for value addition and cold chain infrastructure. It also provides special 
assistance to start-ups, Farmer Producer Organizations (FPOs), Self-Help Groups (SHGs), and 
farmers to adopt modern technologies and establish decentralized processing and storage 
facilities. Through this policy, the state has witnessed significant expansion in the food 
processing sector, leading to increased employment opportunities and enhanced 
competitiveness of Uttar Pradesh in national and global markets. 
Economic Impact 
 Establishment of Mega Food Parks and Agro Parks leading to large-scale investment and job creation. 
 Promotion of exports of processed food products from the state, resulting in foreign exchange earnings. 
 Encouragement of decentralized processing and storage, leading to increased income and opportunities 
in rural areas. 
 Improvement in the quality and shelf life of agricultural products through value addition and cold chain 
infrastructure. 
 Inclusive growth and promotion of entrepreneurship through special subsidies for women entrepreneurs 
and start-ups. 
Uttar Pradesh Dairy Development & Milk Products & Promotion Policy 
2022 
The Uttar Pradesh Dairy Farm and Product Development Policy 2022 aims to promote milkbased industries in the state and attract capital investment of Rs. 5,000 Crore over the next five years. 
Under this policy, financial incentives are provided for the establishment of milk processing plants, 
animal feed units, milk chilling centres, bulk milk coolers, refrigerated vans, and value-added product 
units. Key features of the policy include capital investment subsidies, interest subsidies, support for 
quality control equipment, development of cold value chains, market development and brand 
promotion, export incentives, concessions in patent registration fees, and relief in electricity and 
stamp duty charges. This policy has enabled the dairy industry to adopt modern technology, enhance 
production capacity, and strengthen its position in global competition.

Economic Impact 
 Direct and indirect employment generation providing opportunities for rural youth and entrepreneurs. 
 Increase in farmers’ and dairy producers’ income through rural empowerment. 
 Infrastructure development such as cold value chains, milk chilling centres, and modern processing 
units. 
 Promotion of exports, enhancing the reach of the state’s dairy products in national and international 
markets. 
 Encouragement of innovation and branding, ensuring the long-term growth of the Uttar Pradesh dairy 
industry. 
Uttar Pradesh Poultry Development Policy 2022 
The Uttar Pradesh Poultry Development Policy 2022 has been implemented with the 
objective of making the state self-reliant in poultry meat and egg production while also promoting 
exports. The policy aims to at least double farmers’ income through poultry farming and create new 
employment opportunities. Under this policy, poultry units are provided with facilities such as 
interest subsidies, full reimbursement of electricity charges, exemption from stamp duty on land, a 
dedicated portal, and a Project Facilitation Centre. In addition, capacity building of beneficiaries is 
ensured through entrepreneurship development and technical training, thereby strengthening the 
poultry sector. 
Economic Impact 
 Promotion of investment and entrepreneurship, leading to the expansion of the poultry industry. 
 Direct and indirect employment generation, creating opportunities for rural youth and farmers. 
 Increase in egg and meat production, making the state self-reliant and export-oriented. 
 Growth in agricultural income, strengthening the economic condition of farmers. 
 Technical training and capacity building, improving the quality and competitiveness of the industry. 
Uttar Pradesh Agriculture Export Policy 2019 (First Amendment 2021) 
The Uttar Pradesh Agricultural Export Policy 2019 (Amendment-2021) aims to provide new 
direction to the export of agricultural produce and processed products from the state, enhance 
farmers’ income, and make Uttar Pradesh competitive in the global market. Under this policy, the 
creation of agricultural export clusters is encouraged, with financial assistance ranging from Rs. 10 
Lakh to Rs. 40 Lakh depending on the area. Additional funds for cluster expansion, phased incentives 
for export growth, and facilities such as transport subsidies are provided to farmers and entrepreneurs. 
By strengthening the quality of agricultural products, value addition, and export capacity, this policy 
represents a concrete step toward making the state a major hub for agricultural exports. 
 Economic Impact 
 Doubling of farmers’ income, thereby strengthening the rural economy. 
 Increase in exports, expanding the reach of the state’s agricultural products in national and international 
markets. 
 Improvement in global competitiveness, enhancing the brand value of Uttar Pradesh’s agricultural 
products. 
 Cluster-based development, leading to greater efficiency in production, processing, and marketing. 
 Transport subsidies and ecosystem support, reducing export costs and increasing profitability.

2. Policies related to the Industrial and Manufacturing 
Sector 
Recognizing the industrial and manufacturing sector as the engine of the state’s development 
journey, the Government of Uttar Pradesh has announced numerous policies to promote investment, 
technological innovation, and entrepreneurship. Through these policies, the state aims to establish 
itself as a modern manufacturing hub, expand employment opportunities, and assume a leading role 
in global competitiveness. 
Uttar Pradesh Industrial Investment & Employment Promotion Policy 
2022 
The Uttar Pradesh Industrial Investment & Employment Promotion Policy, 2022 aims to 
establish the state as a competitive investment destination at both the national and international levels, 
create employment opportunities, and promote sustainable, inclusive, and balanced economic 
growth. Under this policy, large, mega, super‑mega, and ultra‑mega units are provided with benefits 
such as stamp duty exemption, capital subsidy, SGST reimbursement, PLI top‑up incentives, 
financial assistance for centres of excellence, and special concessions for infrastructure projects. 
These provisions represent concrete steps toward attracting investors, strengthening industrial 
infrastructure, and developing the state as an industrial hub. Under this policy, approximately Rs. 3.9 
Lakh Crore worth of investment proposals have been received through 139 applications for the 
‘Letter of Comfort.’ Of these, 60 applications with investment proposals amounting to about Rs. 
48,063 Crore have already been approved, including major investors such as Varun Beverages and 
Amba Shakti. 
Economic Impact 
 Development of private industrial parks, leading to increased investment and employment opportunities. 
 Promotion of new research and development, resulting in technological innovation and improved 
competitiveness. 
 Encouragement of regional development and investment, ensuring balanced industrial expansion and 
inclusive economic growth. 
 Attraction of large-scale capital investment, thereby enhancing the state’s industrial capacity and 
production. 
 Drawing global investors, positioning Uttar Pradesh as an industrial destination at both national and 
international levels. 
 
Uttar Pradesh Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSME) 
Promotion Policy, 2022 
The Uttar Pradesh Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSME) Promotion Policy, 2022 
aims to encourage the establishment of new MSME units in the state, thereby fostering regional 
economic and social balance and positioning Uttar Pradesh as an attractive investment destination. 
Under this policy, facilities such as capital subsidy, interest subsidy, infrastructural support for 
industrial parks, stamp duty exemption, and additional incentives for women and Scheduled 
Caste/Scheduled Tribe entrepreneurs are provided. This has not only promoted entrepreneurship but

has also ensured the expansion of industrial infrastructure and balanced development of the backward 
regions of the state.

 Promotion of industrial development, leading to increased production capacity and investment. 
 Encouragement of quality improvement, modern technology, and competitiveness among MSMEs. 
 Development of Purvanchal and Bundelkhand regions, ensuring regional balance and employment 
generation. 
 Promotion of women and disadvantaged entrepreneurs, fostering inclusive economic growth. 
 Expansion of Industrial Parks and Complexes, strengthening infrastructural facilities. 
Uttar Pradesh Textile and Garmenting Policy 2022 
The Uttar Pradesh Textile and Garments Policy, 2022 aims to establish the state as a global 
textile manufacturing hub and to promote the sustainable development of the entire value chain. 
Under this policy, new textile and garment units, silk industry enterprises, handloom and fabric 
product units engaged in production, design, marketing, and export are provided with facilities such 
as land cost reimbursement, stamp duty exemption, capital subsidy, interest subsidy, and export 
freight reimbursement. In particular, higher rates of subsidy have been extended in the Purvanchal 
and Bundelkhand regions to encourage regional balance and employment generation. By linking the 
state’s textile industry with modern technology, investment, and global competitiveness, this policy 
is laying the foundation for long‑term development.

 Promotion of the silk industry, enabling Uttar Pradesh to develop as a global textile manufacturing hub. 
 Increase in the income of handloom and powerloom weavers, strengthening rural and traditional

 Development of integrated textile parks, enhancing efficiency in production, processing, and marketing. 
 Encouragement of exports, expanding the reach and competitiveness of the state’s textile products in 
international markets. 
 Employment generation and regional development, particularly through industrial expansion in 
Purvanchal and Bundelkhand. 
Uttar Pradesh Semiconductor Policy, 2024 
The Uttar Pradesh Semiconductor Policy, 2024 aims to create a favourable ecosystem for 
the semiconductor industry in the state and to attract investors, thereby positioning Uttar Pradesh as 
a leading hub in this sector. Under this policy, projects such as semiconductor fabs, display fabs, 
sensor fabs, ATMP (Assembly, Testing, Marking, and Packaging) units, and outsourced assembly 
and test facilities are provided with incentives including capital support, interest subsidy, land cost 
subsidy, stamp duty and electricity duty exemptions, financial assistance for centres of excellence, 
reimbursement of patent registration fees, and support for worker housing development. This policy 
represents a concrete step toward making the state a centre of high‑tech manufacturing, research, and 
innovation. 
Economic Impact 
 Development of world class infrastructure, creating a strong ecosystem for the semiconductor industry. 
 Promotion of research and development, leading to technological innovation and enhanced 
competitiveness.

Uttar Pradesh Electronics Manufacturing Policy 2020 (Amend. 2022) 
The Uttar Pradesh Electronics Manufacturing Policy, 2020 (Amendment 2022) aims to 
create a world‑class ESDM (Electronics System Design and Manufacturing) ecosystem in the state, 
empower MSME enterprises, and generate more than 400,000 employment opportunities. Under this 
policy, large investors are provided with incentives such as capital subsidy, interest subsidy, stamp 
duty exemption, patent cost reimbursement, logistics subsidy, and additional benefits in focus areas 
like Defence electronics, strategic electronics, and robotics. In addition, reconstruction, repair, and 
renovation units are also extended similar benefits. This policy represents a concrete initiative to 
make Uttar Pradesh a leading centre of electronics manufacturing and to advance its position in global 
competitiveness.

16. Vision of Viksit Bharat -Viksit Uttar 
Pradesh @2047 
 
 During the Amrit Mahotsav year of India’s independence, the entire nation remained deeply 
connected with the spirit of national leadership. At that time, the Hon’ble Prime Minister placed 
before the citizens of the country a set of resolutions, the most significant and inspiring of which was 
the resolve to establish India as a developed nation by the year 2047. It is evident that the country 
will become developed only when all States play their vital role in this direction. Uttar Pradesh, being 
the most populous State of the country, has both the opportunity and necessity to contribute 
prominently to this national resolve. To realise the Hon’ble Prime Minister’s proud and 
welfare-oriented vision within the State, the Hon’ble Chief Minister promptly decided to organise a 
wide-ranging deliberation on the concept of 
Uttar Pradesh: Vision @2047 and pledged to 
give concrete shape to this unique development 
vision through public participation. In this 
sequence, a historic 24-hour session of the Uttar 
Pradesh Legislature was held on 13-14 August 
2025 for Viksit Uttar Pradesh: Vision @2047. 
On this occasion, the Hon’ble Chief Minister 
called upon the people, stating that “If India 
today is a bright spot for the world, then Uttar 
Pradesh is the key State driving India’s growth.” 
Today, Uttar Pradesh does not depend on others

In the Development Vision of Uttar Pradesh, priority has been accorded to agricultural innovation, 
livestock and fisheries growth, modern infrastructure such as expressways, waterways, and air 
connectivity, green energy including hydrogen and nuclear power, expansion of industries and 
MSMEs, digital revolution and IT advancement, revival of cultural heritage, urban and rural 
development, social welfare and inclusive upliftment, world-class healthcare services, quality 
education and skill development, as well as security and good governance. These focus areas are 
intended to make the State prosperous, empowered, and a model of comprehensive development. 
For the consolidation of the Vision Document, short-term goals up to 2029-30 include 
enhancing agricultural productivity, expanding scientific techniques, promoting crop diversification, 
encouraging storage and exports, and increasing farmers’ incomes. By 2035-36, the focus will be on 
agricultural innovation, research and development, and expansion of the food processing sector 
through mega food parks, cold chains, packaging hubs, mini processing units, and FPOs, thereby 
positioning the State as an export hub. By 2046-47, the target is to advance Uttar Pradesh towards a 
six-trillion-dollar economy, raise per capita income to at least the national average or higher, and

State a leading region of India.

 Key Highlights of the Discussion held on 13-14 August 2025 for setting the targets of Uttar Pradesh Vision 2047 
To establish the State’s economy as the most developed in the country and raise the per capita income above 
the national average. 
Achieve the goal of Zero Poverty, ensure agricultural prosperity and improve farmers’ conditions, and 
position the State as a preferred global destination for capital investment. 
Provide quality and employment-oriented education for all, establish world-class medical facilities in the 
State, and increase women’s participation in the workforce to at least 60%. 
Develop world-class infrastructure, make Gram Panchayats economically self-reliant, enhance the use of 
space technology in development, and ensure environmental protection and enrichment. 
Transform the State into an Information Technology, Logistics, and Industrial Hub; modernize and empower 
it through digitalization; and promote cottage industries in villages. 
Increase afforestation to reduce greenhouse gas and carbon dioxide emissions, and undertake river 
channelization to address floods, landslides, soil erosion, and related problems. 
Achieve the target of self-reliance by 2027, increase revenue from existing sources, augment resources, and 
reduce dependence on the Central Government and borrowings. 
Curb tax evasion through digital platforms, AI, and technology, and raise the State’s revenue receipts from 
about 40% to over 60%. 
Make special efforts to increase non-tax revenue receipts (currently around 3%), reduce the debt burden of 
nearly 30% of GSDP step by step to 20%, and introduce Climate Budgeting, Green Budget, Pink Budget, 
and Child Budget in the State’s budget. 
Reduce expenditure on general services, increase spending on social and economic services, raise capital 
outlay from about 18% of total expenditure to 30%, and fully leverage schemes such as the Government of 
India’s Scheme for Special Assistance to States for Capital Investment to accelerate the economy. 
Create productive assets through increased capital outlay, thereby promoting industrialization and 
employment generation. 
Raise the State’s development expenditure from about 60% of total expenditure to 70%, promote Research 
and Development, and allocate adequate budget for achieving SDG goals. 
Strengthen MSMEs, include more products under the One District- One Product scheme, and establish the 
State as a leading exporter in the country. 
Develop a robust and dynamic start-up ecosystem to accelerate economic growth and generate employment. 
Prepare a planned development strategy by dividing the State into four regions: Western, Central, Eastern, 
and Bundelkhand. 
Develop Bundelkhand as a Special Investment Region through initiatives such as the Defence Corridor, 
Pharma Park, Solar Park, Heritage Tourism, and establishment of a Dairy Complex, with scope for further 
expansion. 
Establish Jewar International Airport, a 1000-acre Film City, a Global Tech Hub, and a Special Education 
Zone in Western Uttar Pradesh. 
For the Eastern region, establish the Buddha Trail, Special Education Zone, Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Tirth 
Kshetra, Special Agricultural Economic Zone, Research and Development Centre, and an International 
Stadium. 
Include Central Uttar Pradesh in the Special Investment Region, with projects such as a Leather Park, 
Drone and Robotics Hub, AI City, and promotion of Pharma and Textile Parks. 
The State Government has adopted the agenda of Developed India’s Four Pillars- Economic 
Competitiveness, Security, Global Connectivity, and Good Governance placing the State firmly on the path 
of rapid economic growth.

 Workshop for the Vision Agenda, engaging nearly 500 eminent

To realise the concept of Developed India @2047, the Government of Uttar Pradesh has 
resolved to transform the State into a developed, self-reliant, inclusive, and globally respected entity 
by the year 2047. For achieving this goal, the practical and policy-oriented insights, experience, and 
administrative competence of retired senior officers from administration, police, agriculture, 
forestry, irrigation, education, health, science, and engineering, along with eminent persons, will 
prove instrumental in strategy formulation. With this objective, the campaign “Samarth Uttar 
Pradesh- Viksit Uttar Pradesh @2047” has been launched. Under this initiative, a one-day 
orientation workshop with nearly 500 eminent participants was held in Lucknow on 03 
September 2025, followed by two-day district-level visits and dialogue programmes (on 08 and 09 
September 2025). During these, feedback was collected from students, teachers, entrepreneurs, 
farmers, voluntary organisations, labour unions, media, and the general public.

279 
Samarth Uttar Pradesh- Viksit Uttar Pradesh @2047 Campaign 
for Ensuring Maximum Public Participation 
 Under the ‘Samarth Uttar Pradesh- Viksit Uttar Pradesh @2047’ campaign, a portal and QR 
code were developed for the period from 05 September 2025 to 05 October 2025. Through this, each 
participant/individual was required to log in, select a sector/subject, and submit three significant 
suggestions towards the farsighted Vision @2047. To ensure maximum public participation, 
extensive publicity was undertaken at the district, tehsil, and development block levels. Hoardings 
with QR codes were installed, Gram Panchayat-level meetings were organised, and feedback was 
collected through newspapers, social media, television, and other channels. In addition, District 
Magistrates in every district made special efforts to obtain maximum feedback from the public. 
A historic initiative of broad-based public participation and dialogue has been undertaken 
for the creation of Viksit Uttar Pradesh @2047. On 3 September 2025, an orientation workshop was 
organised with more than 400 retired IAS and IPS officers, academicians, agricultural scientists, and 
other eminent persons. Subsequently, across all 75 districts, these eminent persons engaged in 
dialogue with educational institutions, entrepreneurs, women self-help groups, labour organisations, 
and traders, thereby obtaining valuable suggestions. 
To incorporate public representatives into the Vision Document, on 26 September 2025 
Hon’ble Chief Minister held a virtual dialogue with more than 57,000 Gram Pradhans. In 
continuation, during the last week of September, detailed discussions were also conducted with 
District Panchayat Chairpersons and Members, Mayors and Councillors of Municipal Corporations, 
Chairpersons and Members of Municipal Councils and Nagar Panchayats, as well as Block 
Pramukhs. 
 
Special sessions were organised at the levels of District Panchayats, Municipal Corporations, 
Municipal Councils, Block Panchayats, and Nagar Panchayats to deliberate on the Vision Document. 
Suggestions were also received from nearly 350 institutions and 150 experts working in diverse 
fields. Best practices and Vision Documents of other States were studied and incorporated as well. 
In total, 9,770,696 suggestions were received, of which more than 3.5 million came from women and 
over 7.5 million from rural areas. Among the contributors, youth below 31 years of age accounted

280 
for the highest participation (over 50%). The majority of suggestions pertained to three key sectors, 
agriculture, education, and urban and rural development. 
 
In the next phase, sessions focused on Viksit Uttar Pradesh @2047 will be organised in 
every district, wherein discussions will be held on the comprehensive vision keeping in view the 
specific needs and characteristics of each district. This initiative is emerging as a powerful people’s 
movement that will guide the State towards its future direction. 
For all districts, suggestions were received from selected eminent persons, academicians, 
subject experts, teachers, entrepreneurs, various organisations, and the general public, covering 
nearly 9.8 million families. These inputs are being utilised to finalise the Targeted Action Plan for 
the Vision of Viksit Uttar Pradesh as part of Viksit Bharat 2047.

SDG Performance: Uttar Pradesh at a Glance 
The Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) are an ambitious, inclusive, and universal 
global commitment aimed at creating an equitable, just, and secure world for all. These goals are 
anchored in the core principles of holistic development of individuals, the planet, and prosperity, 
structured around the five dimensions of the SDGs People, Prosperity, Peace, Partnership, and Planet. 
Uttar Pradesh has emerged as a leading state in the effective implementation and monitoring of the 
Sustainable Development Goals. The state remains firmly committed to achieving the targets set 
under the SDGs. To evaluate the progress of states, NITI Aayog, Government of India, releases the 
SDG India Index. Uttar Pradesh has demonstrated unprecedented and continuous improvement in its 
performance in this Index. 
 
1.1: Performance of the State in the SDG India Index 
In the SDG India Index 2020-21 (June 2021), the state was included in the Performer 
Category. In the SDG India Index 2023-24 (July 2024), the state advanced to the Front Runner 
Category. The journey from the 29th to the 18th position demonstrates that the state has not only 
focused on priority areas but has also implemented significant schemes and policies based on them. 
Alongside this, the state has further strengthened its commitment to sustainable and inclusive 
development. Uttar Pradesh has been the fastest progressing state in the SDG India Index over the 
past five years. The state has achieved a remarkable improvement of 25 points, moving from a score 
of 42 in SDG India Index 1.0 (2018) to 67 points in the updated SDG India Index 4.0 (2023-24).
